content.text:
Exactly right. You've reasoned through it correctly. Let me name the pieces precisely.

## What k-NN is

**k-Nearest Neighbors** is a classification algorithm. Setup:

1. You have a bunch of points in some space, each labeled with a class.
2. New unlabeled point shows up.
3. Find the **k closest** labeled points (by some distance metric).
4. Vote: most common label among those k neighbors becomes the new point's label.

That's the whole algorithm. Three ingredients: a space, labeled points in it, a distance metric.

## Why our setup is literally k-NN

Map your three pieces of intuition onto k-NN's ingredients:

| Your phrasing | k-NN ingredient |
|---|---|
| "mapped the map onto some kind of vector space" | the space (= embedding space) |
| "coordinate on the map already" | the points have positions (= embeddings) |
| "fitting something in" | classify new point by neighbors |

Distance metric = cosine similarity (or Euclidean — interchangeable on normalized embeddings). Labels = which grouping each authored node belongs to. New point = the new authored node's embedding.

So when we say "embed the new node, find top 5 closest stored embeddings, vote by grouping" — we're not inventing a method. We're applying textbook k-NN to a labeled set that EVōC produced.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
k-NN is one of the oldest classification algorithms (Fix & Hodges 1951, Cover & Hart 1967 proved its convergence properties). It's "lazy" — no training step at all, just store the labeled points. EVōC's job is to *produce* the labels. k-NN's job is to *use* them. Two algorithms, separate roles, glued together by the shared embedding space. That separation is why the architecture works cleanly: you can swap EVōC for any other clustering algorithm without changing the population logic, and you can swap k-NN for any other classifier without changing the bootstrap logic.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## What EVōC's role is in this story

EVōC is **not** the classifier. EVōC is the *teacher*. It looked at the unlabeled corpus and decided "these N nodes belong together, call them Algorithms; those M nodes belong together, call them Compilers; ..." After EVōC's done, the labels exist in the substrate as `dcterms:subject` triples on each authored node.

Population doesn't need EVōC anymore at that point. It just needs:
- A way to embed new text (same embedder EVōC used during bootstrap — for consistency).
- The stored map of `(embedding, grouping_uri)` pairs.
- A distance metric.

That's literally a k-NN classifier.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is the same separation that powers production ML systems everywhere: "training time" vs "inference time" do different things. Training is where the expensive structure-discovery happens (clustering, learning weights, building indexes). Inference is the cheap repeated operation against the trained artifact. Your bootstrap is training time; population is inference time. Recognizing them as different phases is what makes the loop concern dissolve — they don't share state in a way that creates feedback.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Why this naming matters for the thesis

When you defend the population step, you're not defending a novel algorithm. You're defending the *combination*:
- **Bootstrap** = EVōC + LLM-label + CSO-grounding (each component cited in literature).
- **Population** = standard k-NN classifier against bootstrap output.
- **Loop-closure** = approval gate between them.

Each piece is well-understood. The contribution is the architecture, not the parts. That's a much stronger position than "we invented a centroid-comparison heuristic." Examiners will recognize k-NN immediately and stop asking about classification math, freeing the conversation for the more interesting parts (approval gates, drift behavior, mint vs. discard).

## The "world map" intuition formalized

Your metaphor maps cleanly onto how the literature thinks about k-NN:

- **The map** = a labeled set of points in feature space.
- **Drawing the map** = clustering + labeling (bootstrap).
- **Reading the map** = nearest-neighbor lookup (population).
- **Re-drawing the map** = re-bootstrap (rare, deliberate, destructive).

The world-map framing is also why people sometimes call k-NN "case-based reasoning" or "memory-based learning" — the model *is* the labeled examples themselves, and inference is a memory lookup against them.

Want to keep digging on alternatives (HDBSCAN's native `approximate_predict`, prototype methods like Learning Vector Quantization), or update ADR-007 to lock in k-NN against stored embeddings?

input.old_string: - **Centroid drift risk.** As members are added to a grouping, its centroid moves. A new member that classified as "high confidence" today might fall to "mid" tomorrow. Acceptable under D3's gating (the user approved the grouping, not every centroid value), but worth observing during pilot.
input.new_string: - **Outlier propagation risk.** A single mis-classified member becomes a labeled neighbor for future k-NN queries. Similar new content may then classify into the wrong grouping by following the outlier's vote. A demo that shows the user clicking a `knm:prerequisite_of` node, reading its properties, then running a SPARQL query whose WHERE clause uses that same URI as a predicate, makes the point without any explanation.

### `kn:Edge`

A reified edge. An instance of `kn:Edge` is a single edge in the graph, represented as a node so it can carry properties and be the subject or object of other edges.

Properties:

- `kn:source` — points to the node at the tail of the edge
- `kn:target` — points to the node at the head of the edge
- `kn:type_of` — points to a `kn:EdgeType` node
- optional annotations: `kn:confidence`, `kn:authored_by`, `kn:created_at`, `kn:derived_from`, etc.

Reasoning: instances of `kn:Edge` project back to standard RDF triples via a SPARQL construct rule. See "OWL Reasoning" below.

---

1	# ADR-005: `kn:` Scope Under Reading A
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	**Date:** 2026-04-24
5	**Deciders:** Shizhong Yu
6	**Related:** ADR-002 (system vs domain edge category), ADR-003 (reflexivity foundation), ADR-004 (superseded — tiered `kn:` namespace), VISION.md (§4.1 Reading A, §4.8 Reflexive substrate, §6 Scope)
7	**Supersedes:** ADR-004
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Context
12	
13	ADR-004 attempted to organize the `kn:` namespace into three tiers (bootstrap kernel / system vocabulary / system classes) because the shipped `meta.ttl` had grown to 40+ symbols. The implicit assumption was that the engine would keep accumulating `kn:*` predicates as new features (visual styles, lifecycle, document binding, custom types, view preferences) landed.
14	
15	Subsequent vision work changed the question. VISION.md §4.1 commits v1 to **Reading A**: only user-authored knowledge content lives in the graph. Application configuration, runtime state, rendering preferences, and engine-internal plumbing do not. VISION.md §4.8 narrows reflexivity to a **substrate property**, not a UX promise — the meta-model is *holdable* and *renderable* in the same engine, but the user does not edit it through the editor in v1.
16	
17	Read together, those two principles dramatically shrink what `kn:` legitimately needs to contain. Most of what ADR-004 was trying to organize does not belong in the graph at all.
18	
19	This ADR replaces ADR-004 with a vision-derived scope.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Decision
24	
25	The `kn:` namespace contains **only what is required to ground the substrate's type system and to make the meta-model self-renderable**. Everything else moves out of the graph.
26	
27	### What stays in `kn:`
28	
29	**Bootstrap kernel (4 + 4 — unchanged):**
30	
31	| Symbol | Role |
32	|---|---|
33	| `kn:Node` | Universal node class |
34	| `kn:NodeType` | Type-of-nodes class |
35	| `kn:EdgeType` | Type-of-edges class |
36	| `kn:Edge` | Reified-edge class |
37	| `kn:type_of` | Instance-of relation |
38	| `kn:subtype_of` | Generalization between types |
39	| `kn:source` | Reified-edge source |
40	| `kn:target` | Reified-edge target |
41	
42	**Reflexivity-rendering vocabulary** (the minimum required to mark the meta-model as a containable, traversable, renderable subgraph):
43	
44	| Symbol | Role |
45	|---|---|
46	| `kn:edge_category` | Property on edge-type nodes; values `"system"` or `"domain"`. Distinguishes engine-internal containment edges from user-authored relations. (See ADR-002.) |
47	| `kn:contains` | Structural parent-child edge type. Used by the meta-visualization and by node-as-document binding (see ADR-006). Naming resolved by ADR-006 — `kn:contains` over `kn:sys_contains`. |
48	| `kn:body_ref` | Substrate-to-doc-store binding for node-as-document. Object is an opaque URN the doc store resolves. Added by ADR-006. |
49	
50	This is the entire substrate-level surface. `kn:` is small by design.
51	
52	### What leaves `kn:` (and leaves the graph in v1)
53	
54	The following currently-in-`kn:` vocabulary is reclassified as **application config**, not graph content. It moves to TypeScript/JSON in the frontend (or, where appropriate, to backend code constants) and is not stored as RDF triples in v1:
55	
56	- All visual-style classes: `kn:VisualStyle`, `kn:NodeVisualStyle`, `kn:EdgeVisualStyle`
57	- All visual-style property edges: `kn:color`, `kn:icon`, `kn:size`, `kn:line_style`, `kn:arrow_head`, etc.
58	- Style-applicability edges: `kn:applies_to`, `kn:applies_to_category`, `kn:filter_property`, etc.
59	- Lifecycle predicates: `kn:on_delete`, `kn:exclusive`
60	- Document-binding predicates: `kn:document_id`, `kn:has_artifact` *(superseded by `kn:body_ref` per ADR-006; the body itself remains outside RDF in v1, in a SQLite doc store)*
61	- Engine-cosmetic predicates: `kn:visual_style`, `kn:default_properties`
62	
63	These are app-level concerns. Under Reading A they have no business in the graph. Future versions (Reading B, Reading C) may bring some of them back into the substrate as user-customizable nodes, but that is a deliberate future expansion, not a v1 commitment.
64	
65	### What is deferred (case-by-case decisions)
66	
67	~~The following are *legitimate substrate concerns* but their placement deserves separate decisions, not a blanket ruling here.~~ **Resolved 2026-04-28** (see "Deferred bucket resolutions" below). Original entries preserved for historical record:
68	
69	| Symbol | Question to resolve |
70	|---|---|
71	| `kn:NodeSet` | Set-valued edges: needed for user-content typing? Or deferred entirely for v1? Decide in a follow-up ADR. |
72	| `kn:PropertyDescriptor` and friends (`kn:category`, `kn:domain`, `kn:range`, `kn:data_type`, `kn:allowed_values`) | Property-descriptor machinery: is it part of how the user types their content (substrate-level) or is it engine-internal schema (out)? Decide in a follow-up ADR. |
73	| `kn:owl_semantics`, `kn:derived`, `kn:inverse_edge_type` | Inference-related metadata: probably substrate-level (the user's edges have OWL semantics that drive Claim 2). Likely stays. Confirm in inference-engine review. |
74	| `kn:description` | Descriptive text on type/edge nodes: probably stays (it's *about* the substrate, used by reflexive rendering). Confirm. |
75	
76	---
77	
78	## Consequences
79	
80	### Positive
81	
82	- **`kn:` becomes small and defendable.** Around 10 symbols total, all justified by either the kernel grounding or the reflexivity claim. No more "is this engine plumbing or kernel" confusion.
83	- **Tiering is no longer needed.** ADR-004's three-tier scheme dissolves. There is one tier; everything in `kn:` is substrate-level.
84	- **App config gains a clean home.** Visual styles and lifecycle live in code, where they can be developed with normal frontend tooling, type-checked, hot-reloaded, and tested without round-tripping through Fuseki.
85	- **Reflexivity claim sharpens.** Claim 7 now reads: *"the meta-model — a small, principled, type-system subgraph — is held in the same substrate as user content and renders through the same engine."* That is a tighter and more defensible thesis claim than "everything the engine knows is graph data."
86	- **Vision and substrate align.** Reading A's boundary (graph holds user content only) is now mechanically reflected in `kn:`.
87	
88	### Negative
89	
90	- **Migration cost.** The shipped `meta.ttl` and Stage 5 meta-visualization currently rely on visual-style nodes living in `kn:`. Pulling them out requires either (a) moving the rendering-config elsewhere and adapting Stage 5 to read from there, or (b) accepting that visual styles in the demo are stored differently from how production v1 would store them. Decision deferred to companion-work plan.
91	- **Some reflexivity demonstrations get smaller.** If visual styles leave the graph, the meta-visualization no longer demonstrates "the engine's styling vocabulary is editable as a graph." That demo never matched Reading A anyway, so this is correction, not regression — but it's worth naming.
92	- **Stage 5 documentation drifts.** Current Stage 5 docs and tests may reference `kn:VisualStyle` etc. as graph nodes. Those references will need updating once the migration plan is settled.
93	
94	### Neutral
95	
96	- **The deferred bucket is real work.** Decisions on `NodeSet`, `PropertyDescriptor`, and inference metadata are now explicit follow-up items rather than implicit assumptions buried in `meta.ttl`.
97	
98	---
99	
100	## Companion Work Triggered by This ADR
101	
102	To be tracked in the session todo list and worked through after this ADR settles:
103	
104	1. **Update `META_MODEL_DESIGN.md`:** D3 scope-of-kernel paragraph, D5 namespace table, references to ADR-004 — all need to point at this ADR and reflect the narrower `kn:` scope.
105	2. **Migration plan for visual styles out of the graph:** how Stage 5 meta-visualization sources its rendering config once `kn:VisualStyle` is no longer in `meta.ttl`. May be a deferred task if Stage 5 demonstration is acceptable as-is for the thesis.
106	3. **Audit `meta.ttl`:** mark each predicate as kept / moved / deferred per the rules above; produce a target-state Turtle file.
107	4. **Decide `kn:contains` vs `kn:sys_contains` final naming** (open from ADR-002 amendment fallout).
108	5. **Follow-up ADRs** for the deferred bucket: `kn:NodeSet`, `kn:PropertyDescriptor`, inference metadata.
109	6. **Update `THESIS_DEMO_GAP_ANALYSIS.md`** to reflect the new `kn:` boundary and Stage 5 status.
110	7. ~~**Decide fate of `SCHEMA_REVIEW_HANDOFF.md`** (review item that originally triggered ADR-004; points #1 and #6 are now answered by this ADR; remaining points still pending).~~ **Resolved 2026-04-28: file deleted; its points were absorbed into this ADR's namespace addendum and deferred-bucket resolutions, plus ADR-006 (node-as-document), ADR-007 (categorization pipeline), and `TYPE_VIEW_SPEC.md` (meta-view edge scope). Cross-references updated as part of post-Stage-5 reconciliation Step 9.**
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Open Questions
115	
116	- **Containment edge naming.** ~~ADR-002 deprecated the `sys:` namespace prefix in favor of an `kn:edge_category` property. The remaining naming question is whether the substrate containment edge is `kn:contains` (clean, reads naturally) or `kn:sys_contains` (preserves prefix-style intent for grep-ability). Resolve in a small follow-up ADR or as part of META_MODEL_DESIGN cleanup.~~ **Resolved by ADR-006: `kn:contains`.**
117	
118	- **Where exactly do visual styles live?** Outside the graph is decided. The specific home — TypeScript constants, JSON config file, frontend store — is a frontend architecture decision, not a substrate decision. Defer to frontend redesign.
119	
120	- **Should `kn:edge_category` be a literal property or an edge to a category-type node?** Currently a literal (`"system"` / `"domain"`). For consistency with the "everything is a node" principle the substrate could promote categories to nodes. Probably premature — literal is fine for v1.
121	
122	---
123	
124	## Addendum: Namespace Architecture (2026-04-28)
125	
126	This ADR defined `kn:` scope. It did not address how `knm:` (then named for "meta-instances") fits into the broader namespace ecosystem, nor how user-authored content and external ontologies relate. This addendum captures the namespace architecture decisions made during the post-Stage-5 reconciliation.
127	
128	### Decision
129	
130	The substrate uses a **four-layer namespace model**, where each layer represents a stability gradient and authorship community:
131	
132	| Layer | Prefix | Role | Owned by | Examples |
133	|---|---|---|---|---|
134	| Kernel | `kn:` | Substrate primitives + reflexivity-rendering vocabulary | Engine team (locked at v1) | `kn:Node`, `kn:type_of`, `kn:edge_category`, `kn:contains`, `kn:body_ref` |
135	| Standard library | `knl:` | Engine-required edge types referenced by name in engine code | Engine team (grows by ADR) | `knl:prerequisite_of`, `knl:demonstrates`, `knl:assesses` |
136	| External ontologies | `skos:`, `schema:`, `owl:`, `foaf:`, etc. | Domain and general vocabularies maintained by W3C / community | External communities | `skos:Concept`, `schema:Course` |
137	| User namespace | User chooses (e.g., `cs:`) | Domain-specific types and all user-authored content | The course author | `cs:variable`, `cs:Professor` |
138	
139	The previous `knm:` namespace is **renamed to `knl:`** and **redefined**: it no longer holds general meta-instances like `Concept`, `Principle`, `Course`, `Program`, `Professor`. Those move out — into external ontologies (where standards exist), or into the user namespace (where they are domain-specific).
140	
141	### `knl:` membership criterion
142	
143	A symbol qualifies for `knl:` if and only if **engine code references it by name**. This is the *engine-feature test*:
144	
145	> *"If I delete this symbol, does a shipped engine feature (Linear Traversal, Problem-First Traversal, OWL Inference Pass, derived-edge SPARQL CONSTRUCT, etc.) stop working?"*
146	
147	If yes → `knl:`. If no → external ontology or user namespace.
148	
149	Concrete consequences:
150	
151	- `knl:prerequisite_of` qualifies — Linear Traversal hardcodes it.
152	- `knl:demonstrates` / `knl:is_demonstrated_by` qualify — Problem-First Traversal hardcodes them.
153	- `knl:assesses` qualifies — derived edge produced by OWL inference rule.
154	- `Concept`, `Principle`, `Example`, `Assessment`, `Reference`, `Analogy` **do not qualify** — engine treats nodes generically via `kn:type_of kn:NodeType`. These move to user namespace or external ontology.
155	- `Course`, `Program`, `Professor` **do not qualify** — education-specific, not engine-required. Move to user namespace.
156	
157	Expected `knl:` size: 5–7 edge types. Zero node types.
158	
159	### Duplication with external ontologies is acceptable
160	
161	`knl:prerequisite_of` may overlap semantically with `schema:competencyRequired` or similar standards. No alignment table is maintained. Optional `rdfs:seeAlso` linking is permitted for documentation but not required and not enforced. Reasoning:
162	
163	- Maintaining alignment imposes ongoing semantic-drift checks every time a referenced standard updates.
164	- Duplication is the norm in real RDF ecosystems — every community library re-defines `Concept` because each wants control over canonical types.
165	- Engine team's authority over `knl:` semantics outweighs interop convenience for v1.
166	- Users who care about interop can author their own alignments.
167	
168	### Friendliness layer is the UI, not a DSL
169	
170	The original goal "save users from learning ontologies" is met by **UI-driven authoring**, not by a friendly DSL namespace. The UI:
171	
172	- Presents type pickers populated from `knl:` + selected external ontologies.
173	- Renders display names from `rdfs:label` (with optional UI-config overrides for localization or rebranding).
174	- Maps user clicks to the appropriate URI under the hood.
175	- Hides URI complexity from non-technical authors.
176	
177	This shifts maintenance from "alignment table per `knl:` symbol" to "palette JSON config per UI deployment" — significantly less work.
178	
179	### Engine logic stays in code (consistent with Reading A)
180	
181	This ADR's Reading A boundary (graph holds user knowledge + substrate; app config and engine internals stay outside) extends to **engine traversal/inference/validation logic**:
182	
183	- Engine code references `knl:` URIs as constants (e.g., `LinearTraversal` reads `knl:prerequisite_of` directly).
184	- No `kn:traversal_role` metadata vocabulary is introduced. Engine knowledge of "what edges to follow for a given traversal" lives in code, not in the graph.
185	- Validation rules, OWL inference pre-filters, and UI palette config live in their respective code/config homes, not as RDF triples.
186	
187	This keeps the substrate small and matches the precedent already set for visual styles.
188	
189	### Future work: plug-in traversals (deferred, not in v1)
190	
191	If the engine ever needs to support third-party traversals authored against the substrate, a `kn:traversal_role` metadata vocabulary could be introduced so traversals discover their target edge types via graph metadata rather than hardcoded URIs. This would make the engine truly type-agnostic and strengthen Claim 7. Out of scope for v1 demo.
192	
193	### Consequences (addendum)
194	
195	**Positive:**
196	
197	- Namespace architecture matches RDF ecosystem conventions (multiple coexisting vocabularies with stability gradients).
198	- `knl:` shrinks to ~5–7 symbols, all justified by direct engine-code reference.
199	- No alignment-table maintenance burden.
200	- UI-driven friendliness scales better than DSL-driven friendliness.
201	- Reading A consistency holds across substrate, app config, and engine logic.
202	
203	**Negative:**
204	
205	- One-time migration: existing `knm:*` symbols must be reclassified — most move out of the engine-shipped namespace entirely. Includes turtle files, code constants, ADR cross-references, and gap-analysis tables.
206	- The `knm:` → `knl:` prefix rename touches every authored turtle file. Cheap pre-Stage-6, more expensive after.
207	- Loss of an "engine-shipped type catalog" for non-technical authors. Mitigated by UI palette + external ontology imports.
208	
209	**Neutral:**
210	
211	- Education-specific types (`Course`, `Program`, `Professor`) become user-namespace concerns. The demo curriculum picks its own URIs.
212	- Categories (proposed in queued ADR-007) follow the same membership test — engine-required → `knl:`, otherwise user namespace.
213	
214	### Companion work added by this addendum
215	
216	1. **Rename `knm:` → `knl:`** across `meta.ttl`, all design docs, and any seed data.
217	2. **Reclassify current `knm:*` symbols** per the engine-feature test: identify which 5–7 survive in `knl:`, which leave entirely.
218	3. **Pick education-namespace strategy for the demo:** which prefix the demo curriculum uses for `Course`/`Program`/`Professor` (e.g., adopt `schema:` directly, or mint a demo-local prefix).
219	4. **Update the queued category-system ADR (ADR-007)** to apply the membership test rather than auto-place `Category` in `knl:`/`knm:`.
220	
221	---
222	
223	## Deferred Bucket Resolutions (2026-04-28)
224	
225	The four-row deferred table above (NodeSet, PropertyDescriptor + friends, inference metadata, description placement) is resolved here. The principle applied is from the namespace addendum: **prefer W3C / community standards over invented `kn:*` predicates whenever a standard fits**, and **drop everything that engine code does not read by name**.
226	
227	### Resolutions
228	
229	| Symbol | Disposition | Rationale |
230	|---|---|---|
231	| `kn:owl_semantics` | **Stays in `kn:`** | Engine code reads it to configure the Jena OWL reasoner. Engine-feature test passes. |
232	| `kn:derived` | **Stays in `kn:`** | Engine reads it to clear-and-recompute inferred edges and to exclude derived edges from validation. Engine-feature test passes. |
233	| `kn:inverse_edge_type` | **Stays in `kn:`** | Engine reads it to generate inverse-direction edges during inference. Engine-feature test passes. |
234	| `kn:description` | **Replaced by `rdfs:comment`** | W3C standard exists. Reflexive-rendering reads any descriptive text predicate; switching to `rdfs:comment` costs only a search-and-replace. |
235	| `kn:domain` | **Replaced by `rdfs:domain`** | W3C standard. |
236	| `kn:range` | **Replaced by `rdfs:range`** | W3C standard. |
237	| `kn:data_type` | **Dropped — use `xsd:*` typed literals directly** | RDF already provides typed literals. No invented predicate needed. |
238	| `kn:allowed_values` | **Replaced by `sh:in` (SHACL)** *if needed in v1; check usage first* | SHACL is the W3C standard for value constraints. May be unused in v1; companion-work step 3 below confirms. |
239	| `kn:category` (NodeType meta — knowledge / organizational / supporting) | **Dropped entirely** | Engine doesn't read it. UI/app concern if needed; not substrate-level. |
240	| `kn:NodeSet` and friends (`kn:target_set`) | **Deferred to v2** | Set-valued edges not required for thesis demo. Future ADR if requirement returns. |
241	| `kn:PropertyDescriptor` and graph-native property-descriptor machinery | **Deferred to v2** | v1 uses plain triples plus RDF-star where needed (decision 2026-04-21). Graph-native descriptors return only if v1 limitations bite in practice. |
242	
243	### Final `kn:` Kernel Surface
244	
245	After ADR-005, the addendum, and these resolutions, the `kn:` namespace contains exactly these symbols:
246	
247	**Bootstrap kernel (8):**
248	
249	- `kn:Node`, `kn:NodeType`, `kn:EdgeType`, `kn:Edge`
250	- `kn:type_of`, `kn:subtype_of`, `kn:source`, `kn:target`
251	
252	**Reflexivity-rendering vocabulary (3):**
253	
254	- `kn:edge_category` (system / domain partition)
255	- `kn:contains` (structural parent-child; per ADR-006)
256	- `kn:body_ref` (substrate-to-doc-store binding; per ADR-006)
257	
258	**Inference protocol (3):**
259	
260	- `kn:owl_semantics`
261	- `kn:derived`
262	- `kn:inverse_edge_type`
263	
264	**Total: 14 symbols.**
265	
266	`knl:` holds engine-required edge types (5–7 symbols, identified per the engine-feature test in companion work item 2 above).
267	
268	Everything else in the current `meta.ttl` either moves out of the graph entirely (visual styles, lifecycle, document-binding cosmetic predicates), or is replaced by a W3C / SHACL standard predicate.
269	
270	### Companion Work Added by These Resolutions
271	
272	1. **`meta.ttl` rewrite** (also Step 10 of the post-Stage-5 reconciliation): rebuild `meta.ttl` against the 14-symbol final kernel above. Ejected predicates either disappear or move to `app-config.ts` / equivalent.
273	2. **Search-and-replace across design docs and seed data:**
274	   - `kn:description` → `rdfs:comment`
275	   - `kn:domain` → `rdfs:domain`
276	   - `kn:range` → `rdfs:range`
277	   - `kn:data_type X` → typed literal `"value"^^xsd:X`
278	   - Drop `kn:category` predicates entirely (inspect each call site for replacement need).
279	3. **SHACL-shapes file decision:** before introducing `sh:in` for `allowed_values`, audit current usage. If unused in v1 demo, drop `kn:allowed_values` outright. If used, write minimal SHACL shapes.
280	4. **Update `META_MODEL_DESIGN.md`** §"Meta-property declarations" to reflect the 14-symbol kernel and the W3C-standard replacements.
281	
282	---
283	
284	## References
285	
286	- `VISION.md` §4.1 (Reading A scope), §4.8 (Reflexive substrate), §6 (v1 scope)
287	- `ADR-002-system-vs-domain-namespace.md` (origin of `kn:edge_category`)
288	- `ADR-003-reflexivity-as-foundation.md` (foundational pivot to reflexive substrate)
289	- `ADR-004-kn-namespace-tiers.md` (superseded; preserved for historical record)
290	- `ADR-006-node-as-document-binding.md` (resolves `kn:contains` naming and `kn:body_ref` introduction)
291	- `META_MODEL_DESIGN.md` (D3, D5 — pending update)
292	- `SCHEMA_REVIEW_HANDOFF.md` *(deleted 2026-04-28; points absorbed into this ADR's addendums, ADR-006, ADR-007, and `TYPE_VIEW_SPEC.md`)* — external review that triggered this thread

# ADR-005: `kn:` Scope Under Reading A

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Deciders:** Shizhong Yu
**Related:** ADR-002 (system vs domain edge category), ADR-003 (reflexivity foundation), ADR-004 (superseded — tiered `kn:` namespace), VISION.md (§4.1 Reading A, §4.8 Reflexive substrate, §6 Scope)
**Supersedes:** ADR-004

---

## Context

ADR-004 attempted to organize the `kn:` namespace into three tiers (bootstrap kernel / system vocabulary / system classes) because the shipped `meta.ttl` had grown to 40+ symbols. The implicit assumption was that the engine would keep accumulating `kn:*` predicates as new features (visual styles, lifecycle, document binding, custom types, view preferences) landed.

Subsequent vision work changed the question. VISION.md §4.1 commits v1 to **Reading A**: only user-authored knowledge content lives in the graph. Application configuration, runtime state, rendering preferences, and engine-internal plumbing do not. VISION.md §4.8 narrows reflexivity to a **substrate property**, not a UX promise — the meta-model is *holdable* and *renderable* in the same engine, but the user does not edit it through the editor in v1.

Read together, those two principles dramatically shrink what `kn:` legitimately needs to contain. Most of what ADR-004 was trying to organize does not belong in the graph at all.

This ADR replaces ADR-004 with a vision-derived scope.

---

## Decision

The `kn:` namespace contains **only what is required to ground the substrate's type system and to make the meta-model self-renderable**. Everything else moves out of the graph.

### What stays in `kn:`

**Bootstrap kernel (4 + 4 — unchanged):**

| Symbol | Role |
|---|---|
| `kn:Node` | Universal node class |
| `kn:NodeType` | Type-of-nodes class |
| `kn:EdgeType` | Type-of-edges class |
| `kn:Edge` | Reified-edge class |
| `kn:type_of` | Instance-of relation |
| `kn:subtype_of` | Generalization between types |
| `kn:source` | Reified-edge source |
| `kn:target` | Reified-edge target |

**Reflexivity-rendering vocabulary** (the minimum required to mark the meta-model as a containable, traversable, renderable subgraph):

| Symbol | Role |
|---|---|
| `kn:edge_category` | Property on edge-type nodes; values `"system"` or `"domain"`. Distinguishes engine-internal containment edges from user-authored relations. (See ADR-002.) |
| `kn:contains` | Structural parent-child edge type. Used by the meta-visualization and by node-as-document binding (see ADR-006). Naming resolved by ADR-006 — `kn:contains` over `kn:sys_contains`. |
| `kn:body_ref` | Substrate-to-doc-store binding for node-as-document. Object is an opaque URN the doc store resolves. Added by ADR-006. |

This is the entire substrate-level surface. `kn:` is small by design.

### What leaves `kn:` (and leaves the graph in v1)

The following currently-in-`kn:` vocabulary is reclassified as **application config**, not graph content. It moves to TypeScript/JSON in the frontend (or, where appropriate, to backend code constants) and is not stored as RDF triples in v1:

- All visual-style classes: `kn:VisualStyle`, `kn:NodeVisualStyle`, `kn:EdgeVisualStyle`
- All visual-style property edges: `kn:color`, `kn:icon`, `kn:size`, `kn:line_style`, `kn:arrow_head`, etc.
- Style-applicability edges: `kn:applies_to`, `kn:applies_to_category`, `kn:filter_property`, etc.
- Lifecycle predicates: `kn:on_delete`, `kn:exclusive`
- Document-binding predicates: `kn:document_id`, `kn:has_artifact` *(superseded by `kn:body_ref` per ADR-006; the body itself remains outside RDF in v1, in a SQLite doc store)*
- Engine-cosmetic predicates: `kn:visual_style`, `kn:default_properties`

These are app-level concerns. Under Reading A they have no business in the graph. Future versions (Reading B, Reading C) may bring some of them back into the substrate as user-customizable nodes, but that is a deliberate future expansion, not a v1 commitment.

### What is deferred (case-by-case decisions)

~~The following are *legitimate substrate concerns* but their placement deserves separate decisions, not a blanket ruling here.~~ **Resolved 2026-04-28** (see "Deferred bucket resolutions" below). Original entries preserved for historical record:

| Symbol | Question to resolve |
|---|---|
| `kn:NodeSet` | Set-valued edges: needed for user-content typing? Or deferred entirely for v1? Decide in a follow-up ADR. |
| `kn:PropertyDescriptor` and friends (`kn:category`, `kn:domain`, `kn:range`, `kn:data_type`, `kn:allowed_values`) | Property-descriptor machinery: is it part of how the user types their content (substrate-level) or is it engine-internal schema (out)? Decide in a follow-up ADR. |
| `kn:owl_semantics`, `kn:derived`, `kn:inverse_edge_type` | Inference-related metadata: probably substrate-level (the user's edges have OWL semantics that drive Claim 2). Likely stays. Confirm in inference-engine review. |
| `kn:description` | Descriptive text on type/edge nodes: probably stays (it's *about* the substrate, used by reflexive rendering). Confirm. |

---

## Consequences

### Positive

- **`kn:` becomes small and defendable.** Around 10 symbols total, all justified by either the kernel grounding or the reflexivity claim. No more "is this engine plumbing or kernel" confusion.
- **Tiering is no longer needed.** ADR-004's three-tier scheme dissolves. There is one tier; everything in `kn:` is substrate-level.
- **App config gains a clean home.** Visual styles and lifecycle live in code, where they can be developed with normal frontend tooling, type-checked, hot-reloaded, and tested without round-tripping through Fuseki.
- **Reflexivity claim sharpens.** Claim 7 now reads: *"the meta-model — a small, principled, type-system subgraph — is held in the same substrate as user content and renders through the same engine."* That is a tighter and more defensible thesis claim than "everything the engine knows is graph data."
- **Vision and substrate align.** Reading A's boundary (graph holds user content only) is now mechanically reflected in `kn:`.

### Negative

- **Migration cost.** The shipped `meta.ttl` and Stage 5 meta-visualization currently rely on visual-style nodes living in `kn:`. Pulling them out requires either (a) moving the rendering-config elsewhere and adapting Stage 5 to read from there, or (b) accepting that visual styles in the demo are stored differently from how production v1 would store them. Decision deferred to companion-work plan.
- **Some reflexivity demonstrations get smaller.** If visual styles leave the graph, the meta-visualization no longer demonstrates "the engine's styling vocabulary is editable as a graph." That demo never matched Reading A anyway, so this is correction, not regression — but it's worth naming.
- **Stage 5 documentation drifts.** Current Stage 5 docs and tests may reference `kn:VisualStyle` etc. as graph nodes. Those references will need updating once the migration plan is settled.

### Neutral

- **The deferred bucket is real work.** Decisions on `NodeSet`, `PropertyDescriptor`, and inference metadata are now explicit follow-up items rather than implicit assumptions buried in `meta.ttl`.

## Addendum: Namespace Architecture (2026-04-28)

This ADR defined `kn:` scope. It did not address how `knm:` (then named for "meta-instances") fits into the broader namespace ecosystem, nor how user-authored content and external ontologies relate. This addendum captures the namespace architecture decisions made during the post-Stage-5 reconciliation.

### Decision

The substrate uses a **four-layer namespace model**, where each layer represents a stability gradient and authorship community:

| Layer | Prefix | Role | Owned by | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kernel | `kn:` | Substrate primitives + reflexivity-rendering vocabulary | Engine team (locked at v1) | `kn:Node`, `kn:type_of`, `kn:edge_category`, `kn:contains`, `kn:body_ref` |
| Standard library | `knl:` | Engine-required edge types referenced by name in engine code | Engine team (grows by ADR) | `knl:prerequisite_of`, `knl:demonstrates`, `knl:assesses` |
| External ontologies | `skos:`, `schema:`, `owl:`, `foaf:`, etc. | Domain and general vocabularies maintained by W3C / community | External communities | `skos:Concept`, `schema:Course` |
| User namespace | User chooses (e.g., `cs:`) | Domain-specific types and all user-authored content | The course author | `cs:variable`, `cs:Professor` |

The previous `knm:` namespace is **renamed to `knl:`** and **redefined**: it no longer holds general meta-instances like `Concept`, `Principle`, `Course`, `Program`, `Professor`. Those move out — into external ontologies (where standards exist), or into the user namespace (where they are domain-specific).

### `knl:` membership criterion

A symbol qualifies for `knl:` if and only if **engine code references it by name**. This is the *engine-feature test*:

> *"If I delete this symbol, does a shipped engine feature (Linear Traversal, Problem-First Traversal, OWL Inference Pass, derived-edge SPARQL CONSTRUCT, etc.) stop working?"*

If yes → `knl:`. If no → external ontology or user namespace.

Concrete consequences:

- `knl:prerequisite_of` qualifies — Linear Traversal hardcodes it.
- `knl:demonstrates` / `knl:is_demonstrated_by` qualify — Problem-First Traversal hardcodes them.
- `knl:assesses` qualifies — derived edge produced by OWL inference rule.
- `Concept`, `Principle`, `Example`, `Assessment`, `Reference`, `Analogy` **do not qualify** — engine treats nodes generically via `kn:type_of kn:NodeType`. These move to user namespace or external ontology.
- `Course`, `Program`, `Professor` **do not qualify** — education-specific, not engine-required. Move to user namespace.

Expected `knl:` size: 5–7 edge types. Zero node types.

### Duplication with external ontologies is acceptable

`knl:prerequisite_of` may overlap semantically with `schema:competencyRequired` or similar standards. No alignment table is maintained. Optional `rdfs:seeAlso` linking is permitted for documentation but not required and not enforced. Reasoning:

- Maintaining alignment imposes ongoing semantic-drift checks every time a referenced standard updates.
- Duplication is the norm in real RDF ecosystems — every community library re-defines `Concept` because each wants control over canonical types.
- Engine team's authority over `knl:` semantics outweighs interop convenience for v1.
- Users who care about interop can author their own alignments.

### Friendliness layer is the UI, not a DSL

The original goal "save users from learning ontologies" is met by **UI-driven authoring**, not by a friendly DSL namespace. The UI:

- Presents type pickers populated from `knl:` + selected external ontologies.
- Renders display names from `rdfs:label` (with optional UI-config overrides for localization or rebranding).
- Maps user clicks to the appropriate URI under the hood.
- Hides URI complexity from non-technical authors.

This shifts maintenance from "alignment table per `knl:` symbol" to "palette JSON config per UI deployment" — significantly less work.

### Engine logic stays in code (consistent with Reading A)

This ADR's Reading A boundary (graph holds user knowledge + substrate; app config and engine internals stay outside) extends to **engine traversal/inference/validation logic**:

- Engine code references `knl:` URIs as constants (e.g., `LinearTraversal` reads `knl:prerequisite_of` directly).
- No `kn:traversal_role` metadata vocabulary is introduced. Engine knowledge of "what edges to follow for a given traversal" lives in code, not in the graph.
- Validation rules, OWL inference pre-filters, and UI palette config live in their respective code/config homes, not as RDF triples.

This keeps the substrate small and matches the precedent already set for visual styles.

### Future work: plug-in traversals (deferred, not in v1)

If the engine ever needs to support third-party traversals authored against the substrate, a `kn:traversal_role` metadata vocabulary could be introduced so traversals discover their target edge types via graph metadata rather than hardcoded URIs. This would make the engine truly type-agnostic and strengthen Claim 7. Out of scope for v1 demo.

### Consequences (addendum)

**Positive:**

- Namespace architecture matches RDF ecosystem conventions (multiple coexisting vocabularies with stability gradients).
- `knl:` shrinks to ~5–7 symbols, all justified by direct engine-code reference.
- No alignment-table maintenance burden.
- UI-driven friendliness scales better than DSL-driven friendliness.
- Reading A consistency holds across substrate, app config, and engine logic.

**Negative:**

- One-time migration: existing `knm:*` symbols must be reclassified — most move out of the engine-shipped namespace entirely. Includes turtle files, code constants, ADR cross-references, and gap-analysis tables.
- The `knm:` → `knl:` prefix rename touches every authored turtle file. Cheap pre-Stage-6, more expensive after.
- Loss of an "engine-shipped type catalog" for non-technical authors. Mitigated by UI palette + external ontology imports.

**Neutral:**

- Education-specific types (`Course`, `Program`, `Professor`) become user-namespace concerns. The demo curriculum picks its own URIs.
- Categories (proposed in queued ADR-007) follow the same membership test — engine-required → `knl:`, otherwise user namespace.

### Companion work added by this addendum

1. **Rename `knm:` → `knl:`** across `meta.ttl`, all design docs, and any seed data.
2. **Reclassify current `knm:*` symbols** per the engine-feature test: identify which 5–7 survive in `knl:`, which leave entirely.
3. **Pick education-namespace strategy for the demo:** which prefix the demo curriculum uses for `Course`/`Program`/`Professor` (e.g., adopt `schema:` directly, or mint a demo-local prefix).
4. **Update the queued category-system ADR (ADR-007)** to apply the membership test rather than auto-place `Category` in `knl:`/`knm:`.

---

## Deferred Bucket Resolutions (2026-04-28)

The four-row deferred table above (NodeSet, PropertyDescriptor + friends, inference metadata, description placement) is resolved here. The principle applied is from the namespace addendum: **prefer W3C / community standards over invented `kn:*` predicates whenever a standard fits**, and **drop everything that engine code does not read by name**.

### Resolutions

| Symbol | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `kn:owl_semantics` | **Stays in `kn:`** | Engine code reads it to configure the Jena OWL reasoner. Engine-feature test passes. |
| `kn:derived` | **Stays in `kn:`** | Engine reads it to clear-and-recompute inferred edges and to exclude derived edges from validation. Engine-feature test passes. |
| `kn:inverse_edge_type` | **Stays in `kn:`** | Engine reads it to generate inverse-direction edges during inference. Engine-feature test passes. |
| `kn:description` | **Replaced by `rdfs:comment`** | W3C standard exists. Reflexive-rendering reads any descriptive text predicate; switching to `rdfs:comment` costs only a search-and-replace. |
| `kn:domain` | **Replaced by `rdfs:domain`** | W3C standard. |
| `kn:range` | **Replaced by `rdfs:range`** | W3C standard. |
| `kn:data_type` | **Dropped — use `xsd:*` typed literals directly** | RDF already provides typed literals. No invented predicate needed. |
| `kn:allowed_values` | **Replaced by `sh:in` (SHACL)** *if needed in v1; check usage first* | SHACL is the W3C standard for value constraints. May be unused in v1; companion-work step 3 below confirms. |
| `kn:category` (NodeType meta — knowledge / organizational / supporting) | **Dropped entirely** | Engine doesn't read it. UI/app concern if needed; not substrate-level. |
| `kn:NodeSet` and friends (`kn:target_set`) | **Deferred to v2** | Set-valued edges not required for thesis demo. Future ADR if requirement returns. |
| `kn:PropertyDescriptor` and graph-native property-descriptor machinery | **Deferred to v2** | v1 uses plain triples plus RDF-star where needed (decision 2026-04-21). Graph-native descriptors return only if v1 limitations bite in practice. |

### Final `kn:` Kernel Surface

After ADR-005, the addendum, and these resolutions, the `kn:` namespace contains exactly these symbols:

**Bootstrap kernel (8):**

- `kn:Node`, `kn:NodeType`, `kn:EdgeType`, `kn:Edge`
- `kn:type_of`, `kn:subtype_of`, `kn:source`, `kn:target`

**Reflexivity-rendering vocabulary (3):**

- `kn:edge_category` (system / domain partition)
- `kn:contains` (structural parent-child; per ADR-006)
- `kn:body_ref` (substrate-to-doc-store binding; per ADR-006)

**Inference protocol (3):**

- `kn:owl_semantics`
- `kn:derived`
- `kn:inverse_edge_type`

**Total: 14 symbols.**

`knl:` holds engine-required edge types (5–7 symbols, identified per the engine-feature test in companion work item 2 above).

Everything else in the current `meta.ttl` either moves out of the graph entirely (visual styles, lifecycle, document-binding cosmetic predicates), or is replaced by a W3C / SHACL standard predicate.

### Companion Work Added by These Resolutions

1. **`meta.ttl` rewrite** (also Step 10 of the post-Stage-5 reconciliation): rebuild `meta.ttl` against the 14-symbol final kernel above. Ejected predicates either disappear or move to `app-config.ts` / equivalent.
2. **Search-and-replace across design docs and seed data:**
   - `kn:description` → `rdfs:comment`
   - `kn:domain` → `rdfs:domain`
   - `kn:range` → `rdfs:range`
   - `kn:data_type X` → typed literal `"value"^^xsd:X`
   - Drop `kn:category` predicates entirely (inspect each call site for replacement need).
3. **SHACL-shapes file decision:** before introducing `sh:in` for `allowed_values`, audit current usage. If unused in v1 demo, drop `kn:allowed_values` outright. If used, write minimal SHACL shapes.
4. **Update `META_MODEL_DESIGN.md`** §"Meta-property declarations" to reflect the 14-symbol kernel and the W3C-standard replacements.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The four-layer model maps stability gradients onto namespaces. `kn:` (locked, ADR-only changes) → `knl:` (grows by ADR) → external ontologies (community-maintained, W3C track) → user namespace (free authorship). Each layer changes at a different rate; collapsing them into one "engine namespace" hid that.
- Old `knm:` did two jobs at once: hold engine-required edges *and* serve as a catalog of starter type nodes (`knm:Concept`, `knm:Course`). Splitting those jobs lets each one land where it belongs — engine-required edges in `knl:`, starter types in user-namespace or external ontologies. The starter catalog isn't lost; it just stops shipping inside the engine namespace.
- The 14-count is now the substrate's headline number for the thesis. Anything that pushes past it without ADR justification should look suspicious — that's the whole point of locking the surface.

Map below. Two trees, plus where decisions slot in.

## Two roots

**Design** — `D:\ShiZhong\MyCode\KnowledgeNetworkDemo-design\`
Where decisions and architecture live. No code.

**Code** — `D:\ShiZhong\MyCode\KnowledgeNetworkDemo\`
Where implementation lives. Reads from design docs.

## Design tree (by doc-kind, per CLAUDE.md convention)

```
KnowledgeNetworkDemo-design/
├── VISION.md                              ← thesis intent (one doc, careful edits)
├── ADR-001..007.md                        ← frozen decisions (spine)
├── META_MODEL_DESIGN.md                   ← evolving architecture (substrate)
├── TYPE_VIEW_SPEC.md                      ← normative contract (backend↔frontend)
├── KNOWLEDGE_NODE_MODEL.md                ← design (knowledge-content shape)
├── NODE_INVENTORY.md                      ← data manifest (559 nodes)
├── THESIS_DEMO_GAP_ANALYSIS.md            ← living status (drift-tolerant)
├── _reference/                            ← background reading
├── copilot-session-handoff/               ← previous-session state
└── phase-1..7/                            ← build-stage subfolders
```

**Phase folders map to the 7-stage build plan** (CLAUDE.md):
- phase-1-domain-data — 559 nodes Turtle
- phase-2-type-system — 9 node types, 13+ edges (`TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md` lives here)
- phase-3-layered-views, phase-4-traversal-strategies — view + traversal designs
- phase-5-inference-backend, phase-6-validation, phase-7-evoc — engine layers

## ADR spine (read in this order if lost)

| ADR | What it locks |
|---|---|
| **003** | Reflexive pivot. Types/edge-types/edges all are nodes. The thesis foundation. |
| **005** | `kn:` scope = 14 symbols. Reading A boundary. Namespace addendum (4-layer model). Deferred-bucket resolutions. |
| **006** | Node-as-document. `kn:contains`, `kn:body_ref`. |
| **007** | EVōC + CSO pipeline. Bootstrap + Population split. k-NN classifier. Just rewrote last session. |
| 001 | Backend = C# .NET 8 (still valid). |
| 002 | `kn:edge_category` property (not URI prefix) — amended, still load-bearing. |
| 004 | **Superseded by 005.** Don't read except for history. |

## Namespace mental model (post-Step-10, locked)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ kn:    14 symbols, locked v1            ← engine kernel     │
│        bootstrap (8) + rendering (3) + inference (3)        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ knl:   5–7 edge types, grows by ADR     ← engine std lib    │
│        prerequisite_of, demonstrates, assesses, …           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ skos:, schema:, dcterms:, prov:, …      ← external W3C      │
│        SKOS for groupings (ADR-007), PROV-O for lifecycle   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ cs:    user-chosen prefix               ← user namespace    │
│        cs:Concept, cs:Professor, cs:variable_001            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+ kne: synthesized at query time (type-view edges, not stored)
+ rdf:, rdfs:, owl:, xsd: standard W3C
```

Old `knm:` → renamed `knl:` + scope narrowed. Old `knd:` → collapsed into user namespace `cs:`.

## Code tree

```
KnowledgeNetworkDemo/
├── backend/                ← C# ASP.NET Core (.NET 8), :5000/:5001
├── src/                    ← React + Vite frontend, :5173
├── infrastructure/
│   └── jena/data/
│       ├── meta.ttl        ← 14 kn: symbols (just rewrote Step 10)
│       ├── meta-instances.ttl   ← will need knm:→knl: pass + W3C swaps
│       └── domain.ttl      ← 559 nodes, will move knd:→cs:
├── docker-compose.yml      ← Fuseki :3030, Python EVōC :8001
├── IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md  ← top-level code-side plan
├── PLAN_4WAY_HANDLES_COMPOUND.md  ← UI editing plan (separate)
└── package.json, tsconfig.*, vite.config.ts
```

Memory rule: Stage 5 code rebuilds in Stage 6, so `meta-instances.ttl` and `domain.ttl` drift is OK for now — design docs lead, code follows.

## Where you are right now

Just finished **Step 10** of post-Stage-5 reconciliation:
- `meta.ttl` rewritten to 14 symbols
- META_MODEL_DESIGN namespace table updated to 4-layer model

Sitting in the **Stage 2 → Stage 3 transition** of the build plan (rewrite foundations → domain re-encoding). All major design decisions for the substrate are now stable. Pending companion work (per ADR-005) is mechanical search-and-replace across remaining files.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The doc-kind convention (ADR vs DESIGN vs SPEC) is doing real work here — when you're disoriented, the kind tells you whether the doc is *frozen* (ADR), *evolving* (DESIGN), or *contractual* (SPEC). META_MODEL_DESIGN moves; ADR-005 doesn't. That's what lets you hold the system in your head: decisions stay still, descriptions update around them.
- The four-layer namespace model is a stability gradient. `kn:` changes glacially, `knl:` by ADR, external ontologies on a community cycle, user namespace freely. When you see a symbol, the prefix tells you how often it can move — that's load-bearing intuition for both reading and writing turtle.
- Phase folders + ADRs are orthogonal axes. Phase = *what build stage*. ADR = *what decision*. A single ADR (e.g. 007) can affect multiple phases (here: 7); a single phase folder gathers many ADRs' consequences. When you can't find something, ask "decision or stage?" first.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Want a quick re-anchor read? My recommendation: **VISION.md §4.1 + §4.8** (Reading A + reflexivity-as-substrate) — those two paragraphs are the prose summary of everything above.

Audit table below. Sorted by what's authoritative now vs. historical record.

## Stale-token findings

| File | Stale tokens | Status | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **META_MODEL_DESIGN.md** | `kn:description`, `kn:domain`, `kn:range`, `kn:default_properties`, `kn:visual_style`, visual-style classes; `knm:`/`knd:` in body prose | Active design doc; table already fixed | **Body swap + visual-style block to [DEFERRED]** |
| **TYPE_VIEW_SPEC.md** | `kn:description`, possibly `knm:` in projection examples | Normative contract; backend↔frontend reads it | **Swap deprecated; rename `knm:`→`knl:` in examples** |
| **phase-2-type-system/TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md** | `knm:` for declared meta-instances; possibly stale type list | Per ADR-005 addendum, declared types move to `knl:` (5–7 only) or user namespace | **Reclassify each declared type per engine-feature test** |
| **KNOWLEDGE_NODE_MODEL.md** | Body refs to `kn:description` etc. | Design doc | **Mechanical swap** |
| **THESIS_DEMO_GAP_ANALYSIS.md** | `knm:`/`knd:` in current-state tables | Living status — expected to drift but should reflect locked decisions | **Quick update of namespace mentions** |
| **ADR-002** | `knm:`/`knd:` in original decision text | ADR (frozen) — already amended once | **Check: is staleness historical or contradicting?** |
| **ADR-006** | Mentions `knm:`, `knd:`, `kn:contains` | ADR — introduced `kn:contains` and `kn:body_ref` | **Likely OK; read to confirm consistency with ADR-005 addendum** |
| **VISION.md** | `kn:visual_style`, `kn:NodeSet`, etc. | Thesis intent — careful edits | **Read first; minimal touches** |
| **ADR-007** | n/a | Just rewrote last session | **Skip — verified clean** |
| ~~ADR-004~~ | Lots | **Superseded by 005** | **Skip — historical record** |
| ~~ADR-005~~ | References stale tokens deliberately (it's the resolver) | The authority itself | **Skip — those refs are intentional** |
| ~~copilot-session-handoff/**~~ | Many | History/checkpoints | **Skip — frozen by design** |

## Proposed order (highest-leverage first)

1. **META_MODEL_DESIGN.md body** — finish what we started in Step 10. Affects every reader of the substrate. Mechanical swap + mark visual-style section [DEFERRED→ADR-005].
2. **TYPE_VIEW_SPEC.md** — normative contract; backend and frontend developers read this directly. Stale tokens here cause real implementation drift.
3. **phase-2-type-system/TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md** — declared meta-instance types need ADR-005 engine-feature test applied. This is the biggest *content* decision (not just renaming): which types stay in `knl:`, which move to user namespace.
4. **KNOWLEDGE_NODE_MODEL.md** — design doc; mechanical swap.
5. **THESIS_DEMO_GAP_ANALYSIS.md** — status doc; quick namespace pass.
6. **ADR-002 + ADR-006** — verification reads; only edit if contradicting (otherwise leave as historical context).
7. **VISION.md** — careful read; minimal edits with explicit flag-and-discuss for anything substantive.

## What I'd do *now* if you say go

Start phase 1 — META_MODEL_DESIGN body — since the table is already in front of me and it's pure mechanical work.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Audit-then-execute is the right rhythm for cross-file consistency passes. If I just attacked file by file, I'd miss patterns (e.g., `knm:` reclassification in TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN is a *content* call, not a rename — different cost than a sed). Surfacing the whole field first lets us put the content-call *before* the renames so we're not editing the same files twice.
- ADR-005 is doing double duty — it's the decision *and* the migration plan (its "Companion Work" sections). That's why grepping it for stale tokens lights up: those references are deliberate "before" snapshots, not staleness. ADRs that resolve naming changes always have this property — don't autofix them.
- The `phase-2-type-system` reclassification has architectural weight that the others don't: applying the engine-feature test to `knm:Concept`, `knm:Course`, `knm:Professor` etc. is a thesis-claim-relevant decision (which types is the *engine* opinionated about?). Worth reading the file before swinging.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Go ahead with phase 1?

CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- explain-kn: ⚠️ Deprecated — use /learn instead
- learn: Deep learning companion for a CS masters student + software developer — mental models, theory, trade-offs, and research context to build genuine independence
- scout: Quick reconnaissance — understand what something is, why it exists, and whether it's worth learning deeper
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- caveman:caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by speaking like caveman while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
- caveman:caveman-commit: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Cuts noise from commit messages while preserving intent and reasoning. Conventional Commits format. Subject ≤50 chars, body only when "why" isn't obvious. Use when user says "write a commit", "commit message", "generate commit", "/commit", or invokes /caveman-commit. Auto-triggers when staging changes.
- caveman:caveman-review: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. Use when user says "review this PR", "code review", "review the diff", "/review", or invokes /caveman-review. Auto-triggers when reviewing pull requests.
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- caveman:compress: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance, code, URLs, and structure. Compressed version overwrites the original file. Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md. Trigger: /caveman:compress <filepath> or "compress memory file"
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
