content.content:
1	# META_MODEL_DESIGN
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (Stage 1 complete) — undergoing reconciliation to `VISION.md` + ADR-005
4	**Date:** 2026-04-21 (drafted 2026-04-20; reconciled 2026-04-25)
5	**Author:** Shizhong Yu, with Claude
6	**Depends on:** ADR-003 (Reflexivity as Architectural Foundation), ADR-005 (`kn:` Scope Under Reading A — supersedes ADR-004)
7	**Stage:** 1 of 7 in the ADR-003 build plan
8	
9	> **Reconciliation note (2026-04-25).** This document originally referenced ADR-004's Tier A/B/C structure and treated visual styles as graph-native. ADR-005 supersedes ADR-004 and narrows `kn:` to (a) the 4+4 bootstrap kernel and (b) a small reflexivity-rendering vocabulary; everything else (visual styles, lifecycle, document binding) leaves RDF in v1 and is supplied by app config. Sections marked **[DEFERRED — ADR-005]** below describe Reading B/C future work and are kept for historical/design continuity. The shipped `meta.ttl` audit (Step 10 of reconciliation) will reduce `kn:` to match.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Purpose
14	
15	This document specifies the **meta-model**: the small, self-describing graph that sits at the root of the system. Every domain node, every domain edge, every type in the system is expressed in terms of the primitives defined here. The meta-model is the foundation on which all reflexivity stands.
16	
17	If this document is wrong, every layer above it is wrong. We take our time here.
18	
19	The meta-model must satisfy four properties:
20	
21	1. **Self-describing.** The meta-model describes itself using its own vocabulary. There is no external schema file; the bootstrap is a graph that types itself.
22	2. **Minimal.** Fewer primitives is better. Each primitive must earn its place by making something else expressible that could not otherwise be expressed.
23	3. **RDF-compatible.** The meta-model is loaded into Jena as Turtle. Standard RDF reasoners must be able to reason about it. Achieved by declaring OWL equivalences between our vocabulary and RDF/OWL built-ins.
24	4. **Renderable.** The meta-model must be visualizable by the same frontend pipeline that renders domain data. Type nodes carry visual properties (label, color, icon).
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Design Decisions
29	
30	### D1. Layered vocabulary
31	
32	We define our own vocabulary under the namespace `kn:` and declare OWL equivalences to standard RDF/OWL vocabulary. Reasoners see standard RDF; users and visualizations see `kn:`.
33	
34	Why: gives us clean, consistent, user-facing semantics (`kn:type_of` reads naturally; `rdf:type` is a specialist term) while preserving free OWL reasoning. A user never has to learn RDF to author a new type.
35	
36	### D2. Single fixed point at the root
37	
38	One self-referential statement is permitted at the root: `kn:NodeType kn:type_of kn:NodeType`. This is the bootstrap pin. Every other type flows from it.
39	
40	Why: Russell-style paradox avoidance through a grounded fixed point. This is how Python (`type(type) is type`), Smalltalk (`Metaclass class`), and RDF itself (`rdfs:Class rdf:type rdfs:Class`) handle the same problem. We are not inventing; we are inheriting.
41	
42	### D3. Four primitive node types, four primitive edge types
43	
44	The meta-model bottoms out at exactly four node-type primitives and four edge-type primitives. Every other type (domain or meta) is authored on top.
45	
46	The four edge primitives are `kn:type_of`, `kn:subtype_of`, `kn:source`, and `kn:target`. The first two carry the type hierarchy; the last two reify edges. Nothing else belongs in the kernel.
47	
48	Why: empirically, fewer primitives leave more decisions to the user. More primitives bake more assumptions into the foundation. Keeping the bootstrap kernel brutally small is what makes the reflexivity claim defensible — if the kernel grows, the bootstrap becomes a hidden schema again, and "users author everything above the primitives" stops being true.
49	
50	**Scope of "kernel" (per ADR-005).** The 4+4 count is the **bootstrap kernel**. The `kn:` namespace under ADR-005 also holds a small **reflexivity-rendering vocabulary** required to make the substrate self-rendering — currently: `kn:edge_category`, `kn:owl_semantics`, `kn:domain`, `kn:range`, `kn:inverse_edge_type`. That is the entire `kn:` surface area in v1. Visual styles, lifecycle predicates, document-body binding, and rendering preferences are **not** in `kn:`; they are app-config in v1 (Reading A). See ADR-005 for the full list and the rationale.
51	
52	### D4. Edges are reified from the start
53	
54	We commit to Level 3 reification at the meta-model layer. The `kn:Edge` primitive exists from day one. Domain edges are instances of `kn:Edge`. Level 1 systems that stop at labeled edges are a strict subset of what we support.
55	
56	Why: retrofitting reification later would require rewriting the rendering pipeline, every query, and all stored data. Committing upfront is cheaper than any staged migration.
57	
58	### D5. Namespaces are real
59	
60	The substrate uses a **four-layer namespace model** (kernel → engine standard library → external ontologies → user namespace), plus a synthesized `kne:` for projected type-view edges and the standard W3C prefixes for reasoning. This reflects ADR-005 + the namespace addendum + deferred-bucket resolutions (2026-04-28). The earlier `knm:` / `knd:` split has been collapsed: `knm:` was renamed to `knl:` and narrowed to engine-required edge types, and `knd:` is replaced by a user-chosen prefix that holds *both* domain types and instances.
61	
62	| Prefix | URI (placeholder) | Contents |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| `kn:` | `http://knowledgenetwork.local/meta#` | Engine kernel namespace. **14 symbols, locked at v1:** bootstrap kernel (8 primitives — `kn:Node`, `kn:NodeType`, `kn:EdgeType`, `kn:Edge`, `kn:type_of`, `kn:subtype_of`, `kn:source`, `kn:target`), reflexivity-rendering vocabulary (`kn:edge_category`, `kn:contains`, `kn:body_ref`), inference protocol (`kn:owl_semantics`, `kn:derived`, `kn:inverse_edge_type`). Visual styles, lifecycle, document-body binding, and property-descriptor machinery live outside RDF in v1 (Reading A). Changes require an ADR. |
65	| `knl:` | `http://knowledgenetwork.local/standard-lib#` | Engine standard library. Holds the 5–7 edge types referenced by name in engine code (e.g. `knl:prerequisite_of`, `knl:demonstrates`, `knl:assesses`). Membership criterion (engine-feature test): deleting the symbol breaks a shipped engine feature such as Linear Traversal, Problem-First Traversal, or the OWL inference pass. Renamed from `knm:` per ADR-005 addendum. |
66	| User namespace (e.g. `cs:`) | Author chooses (e.g. `http://knowledgenetwork.local/cs#`) | Domain-specific types **and** all user-authored content. The demo curriculum uses `cs:` for both type nodes (`cs:Concept`, `cs:Professor`) and instance nodes (`cs:variable_001`). Replaces the old `knm:` (general meta-instances) and `knd:` (domain instances) split, which collapses under Reading A. |
67	| External ontologies (`skos:`, `schema:`, `foaf:`, `dcterms:`, `prov:`, …) | per W3C / community | Standard vocabularies imported as needed. SKOS shows up via ADR-007 (groupings typed `skos:Concept`, alignments via `skos:exactMatch` / `closeMatch` / `relatedMatch`). PROV-O marks pipeline-generated nodes. No alignment table is maintained between `knl:` and external symbols. |
68	| `kne:` | `http://knowledgenetwork.local/meta-edge#` | **Synthesized.** Stage 5 type-view edges minted at query time. Not authored, not stored — assembled in the SPARQL projection layer so the type-view uses the same edge-rendering pipeline as domain content. See `TYPE_VIEW_SPEC.md` for the projection contract (inclusion rule, projected predicates, edge ID synthesis). |
69	| `rdf:`, `rdfs:`, `owl:`, `xsd:` | standard | Used for equivalences and reasoning. `rdfs:comment` replaces the former `kn:description`; `rdfs:domain` / `rdfs:range` replace `kn:domain` / `kn:range`; `xsd:*` typed literals replace `kn:data_type`. SHACL (`sh:`) is reserved for value constraints if `kn:allowed_values` proves required (audit deferred to companion work). |
70	
71	**Namespace decision (locked 2026-04-20):** We use non-resolvable placeholder URIs under `knowledgenetwork.local`. RDF treats URIs as globally unique identifiers, not URLs that must resolve. The base URI is stored as a backend config value so it can be changed later without rewriting data. Linked Data / dereferenceable URIs were considered and deferred — the per-install, desktop-oriented usage pattern doesn't need them, and shifting to real URIs later is a config change plus a one-time rewrite if we ever publish.
72	
73	---
74	
75	## Primitive Node Types
76	
77	Four primitive classes. All are subclasses of `kn:Node`.
78	
79	### `kn:Node`
80	
81	The root of the type hierarchy. Everything in the system is a `kn:Node`. Has minimal properties:
82	
83	- `rdfs:label` — display string
84	- `kn:description` — optional longer text
85	
86	Declared equivalent to `owl:Thing` so standard OWL reasoning applies.
87	
88	### `kn:NodeType`
89	
90	A class of nodes. Instances of `kn:NodeType` are the things users author when they add a new category to the system. `knm:Concept`, `knm:Principle`, `knm:Course`, `knm:Professor` are all instances of `kn:NodeType`.
91	
92	Properties:
93	
94	- `rdfs:label`, `kn:description` (inherited)
95	- `kn:default_properties` — list of property names instances are expected to carry
96	
97	> **[DEFERRED — ADR-005]** Earlier drafts also listed `kn:visual_style` as a graph-native property pointing at a `kn:VisualStyle` subgraph. Under Reading A (v1), visual style for a node type is supplied by app config keyed on the type URI; the renderer does not consult `kn:visual_style` triples. The graph-native cascading style design is preserved below under "Visual Style — [DEFERRED]" as Reading B/C future work.
98	
99	Declared equivalent to `owl:Class`. This means `kn:type_of` (below) becomes a class-membership predicate that reasoners understand.
100	
101	### `kn:EdgeType`
102	
103	A class of edges. Instances of `kn:EdgeType` are the things users author when they add a new kind of relationship. `knm:prerequisite_of`, `knm:demonstrates`, `knm:teaches` are all instances of `kn:EdgeType`. (Note: `kn:subtype_of` is a *kernel* primitive — it lives in `kn:`, not `knm:`. Authored edge types extend the system above the kernel; they don't redeclare it.)
104	
105	Properties:
106	
107	- `rdfs:label`, `kn:description`
108	- `kn:edge_category` — `"system"` or `"domain"` (per ADR-002 amended)
109	- `kn:domain`, `kn:range` — references to permitted source/target `kn:NodeType`s
110	- `kn:owl_semantics` — one or more of: `owl:TransitiveProperty`, `owl:SymmetricProperty`, `owl:FunctionalProperty`, `owl:InverseFunctionalProperty`. This is what drives inference.
111	- `kn:inverse_edge_type` — optional reference to another `kn:EdgeType`, used to derive the inverse direction.
112	
113	> **[DEFERRED — ADR-005]** `kn:visual_style` is not a v1 property of `kn:EdgeType`. Edge styling is supplied by app config keyed on the edge-type URI.
114	
115	Declared equivalent to `owl:ObjectProperty` (for the standard kind) or more specific OWL property classes.
116	
117	**Edge types have two faces.** Every `kn:EdgeType` instance simultaneously plays two roles:
118	
119	1. **As a node.** `knm:prerequisite_of` is a graph node. Users can inspect it, style it, attach descriptions, query its neighborhood, traverse it in the type-view. It has an id, a label, a type (`kn:EdgeType`), and properties.
120	2. **As a predicate.** `knm:prerequisite_of` is also an RDF property URI. It appears as the predicate in classical triples such as `knd:Variable knm:prerequisite_of knd:Function`. SPARQL patterns and OWL rules operate on it as a relationship, not a node.
121	
122	Both readings are valid at the same time and on the same URI. RDF permits this because a URI can denote both a resource (node) and a predicate (edge label) without contradiction. This is the structural basis for Level 2 reflexivity: the type system is legible to the engine with the same machinery the domain content uses. A demo that shows the user clicking a `knm:prerequisite_of` node, reading its properties, then running a SPARQL query whose WHERE clause uses that same URI as a predicate, makes the point without any explanation.
123	
124	### `kn:Edge`
125	
126	A reified edge. An instance of `kn:Edge` is a single edge in the graph, represented as a node so it can carry properties and be the subject or object of other edges.
127	
128	Properties:
129	
130	- `kn:source` — points to the node at the tail of the edge
131	- `kn:target` — points to the node at the head of the edge
132	- `kn:type_of` — points to a `kn:EdgeType` node
133	- optional annotations: `kn:confidence`, `kn:authored_by`, `kn:created_at`, `kn:derived_from`, etc.
134	
135	Reasoning: instances of `kn:Edge` project back to standard RDF triples via a SPARQL construct rule. See "OWL Reasoning" below.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## Primitive Edge Types
140	
141	Four edge-type primitives. All are instances of `kn:EdgeType`.
142	
143	### `kn:type_of`
144	
145	Links any node to its type. The ubiquitous reflexive edge.
146	
147	- Declared `owl:equivalentProperty rdf:type`.
148	- Used everywhere: `knd:some_concept kn:type_of knm:Concept`.
149	
150	### `kn:subtype_of`
151	
152	Links one `kn:NodeType` (or `kn:EdgeType`) to a more general one.
153	
154	- Declared `owl:equivalentProperty rdfs:subClassOf` when between `kn:NodeType` nodes.
155	- Declared `owl:equivalentProperty rdfs:subPropertyOf` when between `kn:EdgeType` nodes. (SPARQL-level distinction enforced by the backend.)
156	- Transitive by OWL.
157	
158	### `kn:source` and `kn:target`
159	
160	Reification endpoints. Used only by `kn:Edge` instances. Collectively, these two edges reify a classical triple:
161	
162	```
163	Classical:   knd:a  knm:prerequisite_of  knd:b
164	Reified:     knd:edge42  kn:source  knd:a
165	             knd:edge42  kn:target  knd:b
166	             knd:edge42  kn:type_of  knm:prerequisite_of
167	```
168	
169	Both encodings coexist in the store. See "OWL Reasoning" for how they stay in sync.
170	
171	*(Technically this is four edge-type primitives if you count `kn:source` and `kn:target` separately. They are paired semantically but distinct predicates.)*
172	
173	---
174	
175	## The Fixed Point
176	
177	The meta-model types itself. Here are the self-referential statements, written in Turtle-ish pseudocode:
178	
179	```
180	kn:Node        kn:type_of     kn:NodeType .
181	kn:NodeType    kn:type_of     kn:NodeType .      # the fixed point
182	kn:EdgeType    kn:type_of     kn:NodeType .
183	kn:Edge        kn:type_of     kn:NodeType .
184	
185	kn:type_of     kn:type_of     kn:EdgeType .
186	kn:subtype_of  kn:type_of     kn:EdgeType .
187	kn:source      kn:type_of     kn:EdgeType .
188	kn:target      kn:type_of     kn:EdgeType .
189	
190	kn:NodeType    kn:subtype_of  kn:Node .
191	kn:EdgeType    kn:subtype_of  kn:Node .
192	kn:Edge        kn:subtype_of  kn:Node .
193	```
194	
195	Read aloud:
196	
197	- Node is a type of node of type NodeType. NodeType is itself of type NodeType — this is the pin.
198	- EdgeType and Edge are also types of node.
199	- The four primitive edge types (`type_of`, `subtype_of`, `source`, `target`) are of type EdgeType.
200	- NodeType, EdgeType, and Edge are all subtypes of Node (because everything is a node).
201	
202	This bootstrap is small enough to fit on one page, and every piece of it is expressible in our own vocabulary. This is the reflexive foundation.
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Worked Examples
207	
208	**Authoring convention.** In the examples below, authored Turtle uses `kn:type_of` rather than the RDF shorthand `a` (`rdf:type`). They are equivalent under OWL — `kn:type_of owl:equivalentProperty rdf:type` is declared in the meta-model, and the reasoner bridges them — but the demo, the thesis, and user-facing tooling should speak the project's own vocabulary. SPARQL queries still use `a` where it reads more naturally; the reasoner handles the equivalence.
209	
210	### Level 1: A domain Concept node
211	
212	User adds the node "Variable" to CS101.
213	
214	```turtle
215	knm:Concept  kn:type_of kn:NodeType ;
216	    rdfs:label "Concept" .
217	
218	knd:variable  kn:type_of knm:Concept ;
219	    rdfs:label "Variable" ;
220	    kn:description "A named storage location for a value." .
221	```
222	
223	What the visualization pipeline does (v1, per ADR-005): fetches `knd:variable`, follows `kn:type_of` to `knm:Concept`, looks up `knm:Concept` in the renderer's app-config style map, renders the node. The style does not live in the graph in v1.
224	
225	### Level 2: The edge-type `prerequisite_of` as a node
226	
227	```turtle
228	knm:prerequisite_of  kn:type_of kn:EdgeType ;
229	    rdfs:label "prerequisite of" ;
230	    kn:description "A must be understood before B can be taught." ;
231	    kn:edge_category "domain" ;
232	    kn:owl_semantics owl:TransitiveProperty .
233	```
234	
235	`knm:prerequisite_of` is a node. It has properties. It can be the subject or object of other edges. If a user adds "this relationship was invented by John Dewey," they do that by attaching an edge *to this node*, not by changing code.
236	
237	### Level 3: An actual prerequisite edge
238	
239	Say `knd:variable` is a prerequisite of `knd:function`.
240	
241	Reified form (what we store):
242	
243	```turtle
244	knd:edge_var_func  kn:type_of knm:prerequisite_of ;
245	    kn:source knd:variable ;
246	    kn:target knd:function ;
247	    kn:authored_by knd:prof_smith ;
248	    kn:created_at "2025-09-15"^^xsd:date ;
249	    kn:confidence 1.0 .
250	```
251	
252	Classical form (what reasoners also see, via projection rule):
253	
254	```turtle
255	knd:variable  knm:prerequisite_of  knd:function .
256	```
257	
258	Both forms are present in the store. The classical form enables efficient SPARQL queries (`?x knm:prerequisite_of ?y`). The reified form enables annotations.
259	
260	---
261	
262	## OWL Reasoning
263	
264	The backend invokes Jena's OWL reasoner on demand (per ADR-001 Phase 5 design, which carries forward). The reasoner needs two things from the meta-model to work:
265	
266	**1. Equivalence declarations** connect our vocabulary to OWL's:
267	
268	```turtle
269	kn:type_of       owl:equivalentProperty rdf:type .
270	kn:subtype_of    owl:equivalentProperty rdfs:subClassOf .
271	kn:NodeType      owl:equivalentClass   owl:Class .
272	kn:Node          owl:equivalentClass   owl:Thing .
273	```
274	
275	**2. A projection rule** that materializes classical triples from reified edges:
276	
277	```sparql
278	CONSTRUCT { ?s ?p ?o }
279	WHERE {
280	  ?edge kn:type_of ?p ;
281	        kn:source ?s ;
282	        kn:target ?o .
283	  ?p a kn:EdgeType .
284	}
285	```
286	
287	Run once at startup and after every edit, the projection populates the classical form. From there, OWL semantics declared on `kn:EdgeType` instances (transitivity, symmetry, etc.) drive all downstream inference.
288	
289	This is the bridge. Reflexive storage, classical reasoning. Both in the same store.
290	
291	### OWL profile
292	
293	We target **OWL 2 RL** (the rule-based profile). Every inference our design needs is rule-shaped:
294	
295	- Transitivity (prerequisite_of chains)
296	- Symmetry (is_analogous_to)
297	- Inverse properties (demonstrates / is_demonstrated_by)
298	- Subtype propagation (through `kn:subtype_of` → `rdfs:subClassOf`)
299	- Equivalence assertions (`kn:type_of owl:equivalentProperty rdf:type`)
300	- The projection rule above
301	
302	OWL 2 RL matches Jena's native rule engine. Stronger profiles (DL, Full) would add power we do not use and require bolting on external reasoners (Pellet, HermiT) with more moving parts and worse performance. Weaker profiles (EL, QL) don't cover our needs.
303	
304	If a future requirement genuinely needs a stronger profile, we will document that in an ADR and evaluate the reasoner change then.
305	
306	---
307	
308	## Visual Style — [DEFERRED — ADR-005]
309	
310	> **v1 reality (Reading A).** Visual style for node types and edge types is supplied by **app config** keyed on the type URI (e.g., `knm:Concept`). The graph does not store style triples; the renderer does not query for them. This keeps `kn:` small and removes a class of "config in graph" awkwardness.
311	>
312	> **The design below is preserved as Reading B/C future work.** It describes how a graph-native, cascading style system would look if v1's "structure earned, not imposed" philosophy is later relaxed to admit user-authored theming as first-class graph content. None of it is built in v1; none of the `kn:VisualStyle` / `kn:NodeVisualStyle` / `kn:EdgeVisualStyle` classes ship in `meta.ttl` after the Step 10 audit.
313	
314	Visual style is itself a subgraph, not an opaque blob. This preserves reflexivity (the styling system is inspectable and visualizable by the same pipeline) and unlocks cascading via `kn:subtype_of`.
315	
316	### Style classes
317	
318	Abstract parent plus two concrete subclasses, all `kn:NodeType` instances:
319	
320	- `kn:VisualStyle` (abstract)
321	- `kn:NodeVisualStyle` — subtype of `kn:VisualStyle`. Properties: `kn:color`, `kn:icon`, `kn:size`, `kn:border_style`, `kn:label_position`.
322	- `kn:EdgeVisualStyle` — subtype of `kn:VisualStyle`. Properties: `kn:color`, `kn:line_style`, `kn:arrow_head`, `kn:width`, `kn:label_position`.
323	
324	A `kn:NodeType` references a `kn:NodeVisualStyle` instance. A `kn:EdgeType` references a `kn:EdgeVisualStyle` instance. Type mismatch (an edge type pointing at a node style) is a validation error.
325	
326	### Cascading resolution
327	
328	Style nodes themselves form a `kn:subtype_of` hierarchy. To resolve the effective style for a given type, the frontend (or backend, before serializing) walks from the most specific style node upward through `kn:subtype_of`, taking the first defined value for each property. This is CSS-style cascading, expressed in RDF.
329	
330	Example:
331	
332	```turtle
333	knm:default_node_style  a kn:NodeVisualStyle ;
334	    kn:color "#888888" ;
335	    kn:icon "circle" ;
336	    kn:size 30 .
337	
338	knm:concept_style  a kn:NodeVisualStyle ;
339	    kn:subtype_of knm:default_node_style ;
340	    kn:color "#4A90E2" .
341	
342	knm:principle_style  a kn:NodeVisualStyle ;
343	    kn:subtype_of knm:concept_style ;
344	    kn:icon "diamond" .
345	
346	knm:Concept    kn:visual_style knm:concept_style .
347	knm:Principle  kn:visual_style knm:principle_style .
348	```
349	
350	Resolution for `knm:Principle` yields: `color=#4A90E2` (from concept_style), `icon=diamond` (from principle_style), `size=30` (from default_node_style).
351	
352	### What this unlocks
353	
354	- **Theming.** Swap `knm:default_node_style` for `knm:dark_mode_style`; every type re-skins.
355	- **Shared visual grammars.** All assessment types inherit from a common style parent.
356	- **User overrides.** A user-authored theme subtypes the default.
357	- **Self-visualizing style tree.** The style subgraph is itself renderable by the same pipeline.
358	
359	---
360	
361	## Property Representation — [PARTIALLY DEFERRED — ADR-005]
362	
363	> **v1 reality (Reading A).** Plain RDF triples for property values, and RDF-star where per-value reification is genuinely needed, **are in v1**. The `knm:PropertyDescriptor` class — graph-native definitions of what each property *means*, what types it *applies to*, what data type it *carries* — is in ADR-005's **deferred bucket**. v1 ships without it; property semantics are documented in code/docs, not in the graph. A follow-up ADR will decide whether to promote `PropertyDescriptor` back to substrate-level once the v1 demo exposes the actual pain. The descriptor design below is preserved as the candidate solution for that ADR.
364	
365	We follow the convergent design pattern of reflexive systems (Smalltalk, Python, MOF-in-practice, RDF/OWL native): **property definitions are graph-native; property values are plain RDF literals; per-value reification is available on demand via RDF-star.**
366	
367	### The three layers
368	
369	**1. Property definitions are bubbles.** Every property the system uses has a descriptor node under `knm:`. The descriptor carries what the property means, what values it accepts, what it applies to. Users can inspect, author, and extend these through the graph.
370	
371	```turtle
372	knm:color  a knm:PropertyDescriptor ;
373	    rdfs:label "color" ;
374	    kn:description "hex color used for rendering" ;
375	    kn:data_type  xsd:string ;
376	    kn:applies_to kn:NodeVisualStyle , kn:EdgeVisualStyle .
377	
378	knm:size  a knm:PropertyDescriptor ;
379	    rdfs:label "size" ;
380	    kn:data_type  xsd:integer ;
381	    kn:applies_to kn:NodeVisualStyle .
382	```
383	
384	`knm:PropertyDescriptor` is itself a `kn:NodeType`. Descriptors are ordinary graph data, reachable, renderable, and authorable.
385	
386	**2. Property values are simple triples.** The actual values stored on domain nodes use the property URI as an ordinary RDF predicate.
387	
388	```turtle
389	knm:concept_style  kn:color "#4A90E2" ;
390	                   kn:size  30 .
391	```
392	
393	One triple per fact. No reification. Efficient storage. Standard SPARQL queries work without traversal.
394	
395	**3. Per-value reification is available on demand** via RDF-star, when a specific value needs metadata (provenance, confidence, authorship):
396	
397	```turtle
398	<< knm:concept_style kn:color "#4A90E2" >>
399	    kn:authored_by knd:prof_smith ;
400	    kn:created_at "2025-09-15"^^xsd:date ;
401	    kn:justified_by knd:color_blind_guide .
402	```
403	
404	Only the specific statement being annotated pays the reification cost. Unannotated values remain simple triples.
405	
406	### Why this split
407	
408	Making every value a reified node breaks performance: on 559 domain nodes with ~5 properties each, full reification costs thousands of extra bubbles the graph has to traverse for every read. Making nothing reifiable breaks reflexivity: the system can't describe its own vocabulary.
409	
410	Property descriptors at the definition level give the system full self-describing power without paying the reification tax on every data value. RDF-star gives us the escape hatch for cases that genuinely have metadata worth attaching.
411	
412	### What this gives up
413	
414	- Users cannot (yet) add new property *kinds* purely through the graph without touching the property descriptor bootstrap. Adding `knm:accessibility_rating` as a new property means adding a descriptor (data) and then using it (more data) — no code change, but there's still a privileged bootstrap step.
415	- Formal cardinality enforcement (e.g., "a Concept must have exactly one `label`") is not enforced by this structure; it's enforced by validation rules elsewhere (Phase 6).
416	
417	If these bite in practice, we promote `PropertyDescriptor` to a full `kn:Property` primitive in a future ADR. The migration is mechanical.
418	
419	---
420	
421	## Loading Story
422	
423	On first startup, the C# backend:
424	
425	1. Checks whether the Jena dataset contains the meta-model (queries for `kn:NodeType a kn:NodeType`).
426	2. If absent, loads `meta-model.ttl` — a single Turtle file containing the fixed point plus the primitive types and their properties.
427	3. Loads `meta-instances.ttl` — the authored `knm:*` types (Concept, Principle, prerequisite_of, etc.). These are *data*, not primitives; they live in version control because we ship a default set with the thesis demo, but users can add more.
428	4. Loads `domain-instances.ttl` — the 559-node curriculum (produced in Stage 3).
429	5. Runs the projection rule to materialize classical triples.
430	6. Runs OWL reasoning to derive inferences (prerequisite transitivity, assessment coverage, etc.).
431	7. Marks `/api/health` as `ready`.
432	
433	Subsequent startups skip step 2 if the meta-model is already persisted.
434	
435	---
436	
437	## Set-Valued Edges (Optional — Metagraph Compatibility)
438	
439	*Added 2026-04-21 per metagraph discussion. See `RELATED_WORK.md` (parked in `Thesis/Draft 2/`) §"Metagraphs".*
440	
441	The primitive model defines each `kn:Edge` as having a single `kn:source` and
442	a single `kn:target`. This covers every binary edge type in the thesis demo.
443	
444	**Optional extension:** a `kn:Edge` may instead declare `kn:source_set` and/or
445	`kn:target_set`, pointing to `kn:NodeSet` nodes that enumerate multiple
446	endpoints. This matches the metagraph formalism of Basu & Blanning (2003),
447	where an edge is `(A, B)` with A and B subsets of vertices.
448	
449	```turtle
450	knd:combined_prereq
451	    kn:type_of      kn:Edge ;
452	    kn:type_of      knm:prerequisite_of ;
453	    kn:source_set   knd:nodeset_algo_trio ;   # MergeSort + Quicksort + HeapSort
454	    kn:target       knd:Dijkstra .
455	
456	knd:nodeset_algo_trio
457	    kn:type_of      kn:NodeSet ;
458	    kn:members      knd:MergeSort , knd:Quicksort , knd:HeapSort .
459	```
460	
461	**Status for thesis demo:** Not used. All demo edges are binary.
462	**Rendering:** A set-valued edge visualizes as a *combinator node* that fans
463	out to the set members. Classical-form projection: the edge expands to the
464	Cartesian product of source and target members (authored edge-type rules
465	decide which, if any, combinator semantics apply).
466	
467	This is declared here to keep the door open; the 2003 metagraph work shows
468	hyperedges are compatible with typed, reified graphs and carry useful
469	reachability algebra. The demo reserves set-valued edges as future work.
470	
471	---
472	
473	## Non-Goals and Deferred Decisions
474	
475	This document does not cover:
476	
477	- **Authoring UI for meta-types.** The fact that a user *can* add a new `kn:NodeType` through the same graph API as they add domain nodes is a design constraint, but the concrete authoring UX is a separate ADR.
478	- **Versioning of meta-types.** If a professor changes `knm:Concept`'s visual style, do we version? Out of scope for Stage 1; tracked as a future decision.
479	- **Access control.** Who can edit meta-model instances vs. who can edit domain data? Future ADR.
480	- **Distributed / federated meta-models.** Importing someone else's `knm:*` vocabulary. Conceptually supported by RDF, but no design work yet.
481	- **Performance optimization of the projection rule.** If the edge count grows, incremental projection beats full rebuild. Deferred until we measure actual performance.
482	
483	---
484	
485	## Validation Checklist
486	
487	Before this document is marked Stage 1 complete, we verify:
488	
489	- [ ] Every domain type from prior work (9 node types, 13+1+1 edges) is expressible as instances of the primitives defined here. Walk through each explicitly in Stage 2.
490	- [ ] The fixed-point bootstrap loads into Jena without circularity errors. Tested with a scratch Fuseki instance before Stage 3.
491	- [ ] OWL reasoning over equivalences produces expected transitive closures on sample data. Sanity check: load 3 prerequisite edges in a chain, verify derived transitive edge appears.
492	- [ ] SPARQL queries work against both reified and classical forms. `SELECT ?x WHERE { ?x knm:prerequisite_of ?y }` returns results even though the stored form is reified.
493	- [ ] A proposed domain type change (e.g., "add Misconception as a new NodeType") can be added by writing Turtle, with no code changes in backend or frontend. Confirmed as an integration test in Stage 4.
494	
495	---
496	
497	## Resolved Decisions (Historical)
498	
499	1. ~~Namespace URIs — resolved 2026-04-20: local placeholder, config-driven.~~
500	2. ~~Visual style representation — resolved 2026-04-20 as graph-native cascading subgraph; **reopened and deferred to Reading B/C by ADR-005 (2026-04-25).** v1 styles live in app config.~~
501	3. ~~`kn:Property` primitive — resolved 2026-04-21: Option B (middle path). Property definitions are graph data; values are plain literals; per-value reification available via RDF-star when needed.~~ **PropertyDescriptor partially reopened by ADR-005 (2026-04-25)** — graph-native descriptors are in the deferred bucket; plain triples + RDF-star remain in v1.
502	4. ~~OWL profile — resolved 2026-04-21: OWL 2 RL. Matches Jena's native rule engine, covers all required inferences (transitivity, symmetry, inverse, subtype propagation, equivalence, projection), and avoids the complexity tax of stronger profiles we wouldn't use.~~
503	5. ~~Tiered `kn:` namespace (ADR-004 Tier A/B/C) — superseded 2026-04-25 by ADR-005's small `kn:` (kernel + reflexivity-rendering vocab only).~~
504	
505	---
506	
507	## Status
508	
509	Stages 1–5 of the ADR-003 build plan are complete. Stage 5 is what made reflexivity (Claim 7) demonstrable: `/api/graph?view=type` returns the substrate live from Fuseki and renders through the same pipeline as domain content. Reconciliation of older docs to `VISION.md` + ADR-005 has produced the namespace addendum (ADR-005), the deferred-bucket resolutions (ADR-005), the node-as-document binding (ADR-006), the categorization pipeline (ADR-007), and `TYPE_VIEW_SPEC.md`. The `meta.ttl` audit (Step 10) will reduce shipped `kn:*` symbols to match the small-`kn:` decision in ADR-005.
510

# META_MODEL_DESIGN

**Status:** Accepted (Stage 1 complete) — undergoing reconciliation to `VISION.md` + ADR-005
**Date:** 2026-04-21 (drafted 2026-04-20; reconciled 2026-04-25)
**Author:** Shizhong Yu, with Claude
**Depends on:** ADR-003 (Reflexivity as Architectural Foundation), ADR-005 (`kn:` Scope Under Reading A — supersedes ADR-004)
**Stage:** 1 of 7 in the ADR-003 build plan

> **Reconciliation note (2026-04-25).** This document originally referenced ADR-004's Tier A/B/C structure and treated visual styles as graph-native. ADR-005 supersedes ADR-004 and narrows `kn:` to (a) the 4+4 bootstrap kernel and (b) a small reflexivity-rendering vocabulary; everything else (visual styles, lifecycle, document binding) leaves RDF in v1 and is supplied by app config. Sections marked **[DEFERRED — ADR-005]** below describe Reading B/C future work and are kept for historical/design continuity. The shipped `meta.ttl` audit (Step 10 of reconciliation) will reduce `kn:` to match.

---

## Purpose

This document specifies the **meta-model**: the small, self-describing graph that sits at the root of the system. Every domain node, every domain edge, every type in the system is expressed in terms of the primitives defined here. The meta-model is the foundation on which all reflexivity stands.

If this document is wrong, every layer above it is wrong. We take our time here.

The meta-model must satisfy four properties:

1. **Self-describing.** The meta-model describes itself using its own vocabulary. There is no external schema file; the bootstrap is a graph that types itself.
2. **Minimal.** Fewer primitives is better. Each primitive must earn its place by making something else expressible that could not otherwise be expressed.
3. **RDF-compatible.** The meta-model is loaded into Jena as Turtle. Standard RDF reasoners must be able to reason about it. Achieved by declaring OWL equivalences between our vocabulary and RDF/OWL built-ins.
4. **Renderable.** The meta-model must be visualizable by the same frontend pipeline that renders domain data. Type nodes carry visual properties (label, color, icon).

---

## Design Decisions

### D1. Layered vocabulary

We define our own vocabulary under the namespace `kn:` and declare OWL equivalences to standard RDF/OWL vocabulary. Reasoners see standard RDF; users and visualizations see `kn:`.

Why: gives us clean, consistent, user-facing semantics (`kn:type_of` reads naturally; `rdf:type` is a specialist term) while preserving free OWL reasoning. A user never has to learn RDF to author a new type.

### D2. Single fixed point at the root

One self-referential statement is permitted at the root: `kn:NodeType kn:type_of kn:NodeType`. This is the bootstrap pin. Every other type flows from it.

Why: Russell-style paradox avoidance through a grounded fixed point. This is how Python (`type(type) is type`), Smalltalk (`Metaclass class`), and RDF itself (`rdfs:Class rdf:type rdfs:Class`) handle the same problem. We are not inventing; we are inheriting.

### D3. Four primitive node types, four primitive edge types

The meta-model bottoms out at exactly four node-type primitives and four edge-type primitives. Every other type (domain or meta) is authored on top.

The four edge primitives are `kn:type_of`, `kn:subtype_of`, `kn:source`, and `kn:target`. The first two carry the type hierarchy; the last two reify edges. Nothing else belongs in the kernel.

Why: empirically, fewer primitives leave more decisions to the user. More primitives bake more assumptions into the foundation. Keeping the bootstrap kernel brutally small is what makes the reflexivity claim defensible — if the kernel grows, the bootstrap becomes a hidden schema again, and "users author everything above the primitives" stops being true.

**Scope of "kernel" (per ADR-005).** The 4+4 count is the **bootstrap kernel**. The `kn:` namespace under ADR-005 also holds a small **reflexivity-rendering vocabulary** required to make the substrate self-rendering — currently: `kn:edge_category`, `kn:owl_semantics`, `kn:domain`, `kn:range`, `kn:inverse_edge_type`. That is the entire `kn:` surface area in v1. Visual styles, lifecycle predicates, document-body binding, and rendering preferences are **not** in `kn:`; they are app-config in v1 (Reading A). See ADR-005 for the full list and the rationale.

### D4. Edges are reified from the start

We commit to Level 3 reification at the meta-model layer. The `kn:Edge` primitive exists from day one. Domain edges are instances of `kn:Edge`. Level 1 systems that stop at labeled edges are a strict subset of what we support.

Why: retrofitting reification later would require rewriting the rendering pipeline, every query, and all stored data. Committing upfront is cheaper than any staged migration.

### D5. Namespaces are real

The substrate uses a **four-layer namespace model** (kernel → engine standard library → external ontologies → user namespace), plus a synthesized `kne:` for projected type-view edges and the standard W3C prefixes for reasoning. This reflects ADR-005 + the namespace addendum + deferred-bucket resolutions (2026-04-28). The earlier `knm:` / `knd:` split has been collapsed: `knm:` was renamed to `knl:` and narrowed to engine-required edge types, and `knd:` is replaced by a user-chosen prefix that holds *both* domain types and instances.

| Prefix | URI (placeholder) | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `kn:` | `http://knowledgenetwork.local/meta#` | Engine kernel namespace. **14 symbols, locked at v1:** bootstrap kernel (8 primitives — `kn:Node`, `kn:NodeType`, `kn:EdgeType`, `kn:Edge`, `kn:type_of`, `kn:subtype_of`, `kn:source`, `kn:target`), reflexivity-rendering vocabulary (`kn:edge_category`, `kn:contains`, `kn:body_ref`), inference protocol (`kn:owl_semantics`, `kn:derived`, `kn:inverse_edge_type`). Visual styles, lifecycle, document-body binding, and property-descriptor machinery live outside RDF in v1 (Reading A). Changes require an ADR. |
| `knl:` | `http://knowledgenetwork.local/standard-lib#` | Engine standard library. Holds the 5–7 edge types referenced by name in engine code (e.g. `knl:prerequisite_of`, `knl:demonstrates`, `knl:assesses`). Membership criterion (engine-feature test): deleting the symbol breaks a shipped engine feature such as Linear Traversal, Problem-First Traversal, or the OWL inference pass. Renamed from `knm:` per ADR-005 addendum. |
| User namespace (e.g. `cs:`) | Author chooses (e.g. `http://knowledgenetwork.local/cs#`) | Domain-specific types **and** all user-authored content. The demo curriculum uses `cs:` for both type nodes (`cs:Concept`, `cs:Professor`) and instance nodes (`cs:variable_001`). Replaces the old `knm:` (general meta-instances) and `knd:` (domain instances) split, which collapses under Reading A. |
| External ontologies (`skos:`, `schema:`, `foaf:`, `dcterms:`, `prov:`, …) | per W3C / community | Standard vocabularies imported as needed. SKOS shows up via ADR-007 (groupings typed `skos:Concept`, alignments via `skos:exactMatch` / `closeMatch` / `relatedMatch`). PROV-O marks pipeline-generated nodes. No alignment table is maintained between `knl:` and external symbols. |
| `kne:` | `http://knowledgenetwork.local/meta-edge#` | **Synthesized.** Stage 5 type-view edges minted at query time. Not authored, not stored — assembled in the SPARQL projection layer so the type-view uses the same edge-rendering pipeline as domain content. See `TYPE_VIEW_SPEC.md` for the projection contract (inclusion rule, projected predicates, edge ID synthesis). |
| `rdf:`, `rdfs:`, `owl:`, `xsd:` | standard | Used for equivalences and reasoning. `rdfs:comment` replaces the former `kn:description`; `rdfs:domain` / `rdfs:range` replace `kn:domain` / `kn:range`; `xsd:*` typed literals replace `kn:data_type`. SHACL (`sh:`) is reserved for value constraints if `kn:allowed_values` proves required (audit deferred to companion work). |

**Namespace decision (locked 2026-04-20):** We use non-resolvable placeholder URIs under `knowledgenetwork.local`. RDF treats URIs as globally unique identifiers, not URLs that must resolve. The base URI is stored as a backend config value so it can be changed later without rewriting data. Linked Data / dereferenceable URIs were considered and deferred — the per-install, desktop-oriented usage pattern doesn't need them, and shifting to real URIs later is a config change plus a one-time rewrite if we ever publish.

---

## Primitive Node Types

Four primitive classes. All are subclasses of `kn:Node`.

### `kn:Node`

The root of the type hierarchy. Everything in the system is a `kn:Node`. Has minimal properties:

- `rdfs:label` — display string
- `kn:description` — optional longer text

Declared equivalent to `owl:Thing` so standard OWL reasoning applies.

### `kn:NodeType`

A class of nodes. Instances of `kn:NodeType` are the things users author when they add a new category to the system. `knm:Concept`, `knm:Principle`, `knm:Course`, `knm:Professor` are all instances of `kn:NodeType`.

Properties:

- `rdfs:label`, `kn:description` (inherited)
- `kn:default_properties` — list of property names instances are expected to carry

> **[DEFERRED — ADR-005]** Earlier drafts also listed `kn:visual_style` as a graph-native property pointing at a `kn:VisualStyle` subgraph. Under Reading A (v1), visual style for a node type is supplied by app config keyed on the type URI; the renderer does not consult `kn:visual_style` triples. The graph-native cascading style design is preserved below under "Visual Style — [DEFERRED]" as Reading B/C future work.

Declared equivalent to `owl:Class`. This means `kn:type_of` (below) becomes a class-membership predicate that reasoners understand.

### `kn:EdgeType`

A class of edges. Instances of `kn:EdgeType` are the things users author when they add a new kind of relationship. `knm:prerequisite_of`, `knm:demonstrates`, `knm:teaches` are all instances of `kn:EdgeType`. (Note: `kn:subtype_of` is a *kernel* primitive — it lives in `kn:`, not `knm:`. Authored edge types extend the system above the kernel; they don't redeclare it.)

Properties:

- `rdfs:label`, `kn:description`
- `kn:edge_category` — `"system"` or `"domain"` (per ADR-002 amended)
- `kn:domain`, `kn:range` — references to permitted source/target `kn:NodeType`s
- `kn:owl_semantics` — one or more of: `owl:TransitiveProperty`, `owl:SymmetricProperty`, `owl:FunctionalProperty`, `owl:InverseFunctionalProperty`. This is what drives inference.
- `kn:inverse_edge_type` — optional reference to another `kn:EdgeType`, used to derive the inverse direction.

> **[DEFERRED — ADR-005]** `kn:visual_style` is not a v1 property of `kn:EdgeType`. Edge styling is supplied by app config keyed on the edge-type URI.

Declared equivalent to `owl:ObjectProperty` (for the standard kind) or more specific OWL property classes.

**Edge types have two faces.** Every `kn:EdgeType` instance simultaneously plays two roles:

1. **As a node.** `knm:prerequisite_of` is a graph node. Users can inspect it, style it, attach descriptions, query its neighborhood, traverse it in the type-view. It has an id, a label, a type (`kn:EdgeType`), and properties.
2. **As a predicate.** `knm:prerequisite_of` is also an RDF property URI. It appears as the predicate in classical triples such as `knd:Variable knm:prerequisite_of knd:Function`. SPARQL patterns and OWL rules operate on it as a relationship, not a node.

Both readings are valid at the same time and on the same URI. RDF permits this because a URI can denote both a resource (node) and a predicate (edge label) without contradiction. This is the structural basis for Level 2 reflexivity: the type system is legible to the engine with the same machinery the domain content uses. A demo that shows the user clicking a `knm:prerequisite_of` node, reading its properties, then running a SPARQL query whose WHERE clause uses that same URI as a predicate, makes the point without any explanation.

### `kn:Edge`

A reified edge. An instance of `kn:Edge` is a single edge in the graph, represented as a node so it can carry properties and be the subject or object of other edges.

Properties:

- `kn:source` — points to the node at the tail of the edge
- `kn:target` — points to the node at the head of the edge
- `kn:type_of` — points to a `kn:EdgeType` node
- optional annotations: `kn:confidence`, `kn:authored_by`, `kn:created_at`, `kn:derived_from`, etc.

Reasoning: instances of `kn:Edge` project back to standard RDF triples via a SPARQL construct rule. See "OWL Reasoning" below.

---

## Primitive Edge Types

Four edge-type primitives. All are instances of `kn:EdgeType`.

### `kn:type_of`

Links any node to its type. The ubiquitous reflexive edge.

- Declared `owl:equivalentProperty rdf:type`.
- Used everywhere: `knd:some_concept kn:type_of knm:Concept`.

### `kn:subtype_of`

Links one `kn:NodeType` (or `kn:EdgeType`) to a more general one.

- Declared `owl:equivalentProperty rdfs:subClassOf` when between `kn:NodeType` nodes.
- Declared `owl:equivalentProperty rdfs:subPropertyOf` when between `kn:EdgeType` nodes. (SPARQL-level distinction enforced by the backend.)
- Transitive by OWL.

### `kn:source` and `kn:target`

Reification endpoints. Used only by `kn:Edge` instances. Collectively, these two edges reify a classical triple:

```
Classical:   knd:a  knm:prerequisite_of  knd:b
Reified:     knd:edge42  kn:source  knd:a
             knd:edge42  kn:target  knd:b
             knd:edge42  kn:type_of  knm:prerequisite_of
```

Both encodings coexist in the store. See "OWL Reasoning" for how they stay in sync.

*(Technically this is four edge-type primitives if you count `kn:source` and `kn:target` separately. They are paired semantically but distinct predicates.)*

---

## The Fixed Point

The meta-model types itself. Here are the self-referential statements, written in Turtle-ish pseudocode:

```
kn:Node        kn:type_of     kn:NodeType .
kn:NodeType    kn:type_of     kn:NodeType .      # the fixed point
kn:EdgeType    kn:type_of     kn:NodeType .
kn:Edge        kn:type_of     kn:NodeType .

kn:type_of     kn:type_of     kn:EdgeType .
kn:subtype_of  kn:type_of     kn:EdgeType .
kn:source      kn:type_of     kn:EdgeType .
kn:target      kn:type_of     kn:EdgeType .

kn:NodeType    kn:subtype_of  kn:Node .
kn:EdgeType    kn:subtype_of  kn:Node .
kn:Edge        kn:subtype_of  kn:Node .
```

Read aloud:

- Node is a type of node of type NodeType. NodeType is itself of type NodeType — this is the pin.
- EdgeType and Edge are also types of node.
- The four primitive edge types (`type_of`, `subtype_of`, `source`, `target`) are of type EdgeType.
- NodeType, EdgeType, and Edge are all subtypes of Node (because everything is a node).

This bootstrap is small enough to fit on one page, and every piece of it is expressible in our own vocabulary. This is the reflexive foundation.

---

## Worked Examples

**Authoring convention.** In the examples below, authored Turtle uses `kn:type_of` rather than the RDF shorthand `a` (`rdf:type`). They are equivalent under OWL — `kn:type_of owl:equivalentProperty rdf:type` is declared in the meta-model, and the reasoner bridges them — but the demo, the thesis, and user-facing tooling should speak the project's own vocabulary. SPARQL queries still use `a` where it reads more naturally; the reasoner handles the equivalence.

### Level 1: A domain Concept node

User adds the node "Variable" to CS101.

```turtle
knm:Concept  kn:type_of kn:NodeType ;
    rdfs:label "Concept" .

knd:variable  kn:type_of knm:Concept ;
    rdfs:label "Variable" ;
    kn:description "A named storage location for a value." .
```

What the visualization pipeline does (v1, per ADR-005): fetches `knd:variable`, follows `kn:type_of` to `knm:Concept`, looks up `knm:Concept` in the renderer's app-config style map, renders the node. The style does not live in the graph in v1.

### Level 2: The edge-type `prerequisite_of` as a node

```turtle
knm:prerequisite_of  kn:type_of kn:EdgeType ;
    rdfs:label "prerequisite of" ;
    kn:description "A must be understood before B can be taught." ;
    kn:edge_category "domain" ;
    kn:owl_semantics owl:TransitiveProperty .
```

`knm:prerequisite_of` is a node. It has properties. It can be the subject or object of other edges. If a user adds "this relationship was invented by John Dewey," they do that by attaching an edge *to this node*, not by changing code.

### Level 3: An actual prerequisite edge

Say `knd:variable` is a prerequisite of `knd:function`.

Reified form (what we store):

```turtle
knd:edge_var_func  kn:type_of knm:prerequisite_of ;
    kn:source knd:variable ;
    kn:target knd:function ;
    kn:authored_by knd:prof_smith ;
    kn:created_at "2025-09-15"^^xsd:date ;
    kn:confidence 1.0 .
```

Classical form (what reasoners also see, via projection rule):

```turtle
knd:variable  knm:prerequisite_of  knd:function .
```

Both forms are present in the store. The classical form enables efficient SPARQL queries (`?x knm:prerequisite_of ?y`). The reified form enables annotations.

---

## OWL Reasoning

The backend invokes Jena's OWL reasoner on demand (per ADR-001 Phase 5 design, which carries forward). The reasoner needs two things from the meta-model to work:

**1. Equivalence declarations** connect our vocabulary to OWL's:

```turtle
kn:type_of       owl:equivalentProperty rdf:type .
kn:subtype_of    owl:equivalentProperty rdfs:subClassOf .
kn:NodeType      owl:equivalentClass   owl:Class .
kn:Node          owl:equivalentClass   owl:Thing .
```

**2. A projection rule** that materializes classical triples from reified edges:

```sparql
CONSTRUCT { ?s ?p ?o }
WHERE {
  ?edge kn:type_of ?p ;
        kn:source ?s ;
        kn:target ?o .
  ?p a kn:EdgeType .
}
```

Run once at startup and after every edit, the projection populates the classical form. From there, OWL semantics declared on `kn:EdgeType` instances (transitivity, symmetry, etc.) drive all downstream inference.

This is the bridge. Reflexive storage, classical reasoning. Both in the same store.

### OWL profile

We target **OWL 2 RL** (the rule-based profile). Every inference our design needs is rule-shaped:

- Transitivity (prerequisite_of chains)
- Symmetry (is_analogous_to)
- Inverse properties (demonstrates / is_demonstrated_by)
- Subtype propagation (through `kn:subtype_of` → `rdfs:subClassOf`)
- Equivalence assertions (`kn:type_of owl:equivalentProperty rdf:type`)
- The projection rule above

OWL 2 RL matches Jena's native rule engine. Stronger profiles (DL, Full) would add power we do not use and require bolting on external reasoners (Pellet, HermiT) with more moving parts and worse performance. Weaker profiles (EL, QL) don't cover our needs.

If a future requirement genuinely needs a stronger profile, we will document that in an ADR and evaluate the reasoner change then.

---

## Visual Style — [DEFERRED — ADR-005]

> **v1 reality (Reading A).** Visual style for node types and edge types is supplied by **app config** keyed on the type URI (e.g., `knm:Concept`). The graph does not store style triples; the renderer does not query for them. This keeps `kn:` small and removes a class of "config in graph" awkwardness.
>
> **The design below is preserved as Reading B/C future work.** It describes how a graph-native, cascading style system would look if v1's "structure earned, not imposed" philosophy is later relaxed to admit user-authored theming as first-class graph content. None of it is built in v1; none of the `kn:VisualStyle` / `kn:NodeVisualStyle` / `kn:EdgeVisualStyle` classes ship in `meta.ttl` after the Step 10 audit.

Visual style is itself a subgraph, not an opaque blob. This preserves reflexivity (the styling system is inspectable and visualizable by the same pipeline) and unlocks cascading via `kn:subtype_of`.

### Style classes

Abstract parent plus two concrete subclasses, all `kn:NodeType` instances:

- `kn:VisualStyle` (abstract)
- `kn:NodeVisualStyle` — subtype of `kn:VisualStyle`. Properties: `kn:color`, `kn:icon`, `kn:size`, `kn:border_style`, `kn:label_position`.
- `kn:EdgeVisualStyle` — subtype of `kn:VisualStyle`. Properties: `kn:color`, `kn:line_style`, `kn:arrow_head`, `kn:width`, `kn:label_position`.

A `kn:NodeType` references a `kn:NodeVisualStyle` instance. A `kn:EdgeType` references a `kn:EdgeVisualStyle` instance. Type mismatch (an edge type pointing at a node style) is a validation error.

### Cascading resolution

Style nodes themselves form a `kn:subtype_of` hierarchy. To resolve the effective style for a given type, the frontend (or backend, before serializing) walks from the most specific style node upward through `kn:subtype_of`, taking the first defined value for each property. This is CSS-style cascading, expressed in RDF.

Example:

```turtle
knm:default_node_style  a kn:NodeVisualStyle ;
    kn:color "#888888" ;
    kn:icon "circle" ;
    kn:size 30 .

knm:concept_style  a kn:NodeVisualStyle ;
    kn:subtype_of knm:default_node_style ;
    kn:color "#4A90E2" .

knm:principle_style  a kn:NodeVisualStyle ;
    kn:subtype_of knm:concept_style ;
    kn:icon "diamond" .

knm:Concept    kn:visual_style knm:concept_style .
knm:Principle  kn:visual_style knm:principle_style .
```

Resolution for `knm:Principle` yields: `color=#4A90E2` (from concept_style), `icon=diamond` (from principle_style), `size=30` (from default_node_style).

### What this unlocks

- **Theming.** Swap `knm:default_node_style` for `knm:dark_mode_style`; every type re-skins.
- **Shared visual grammars.** All assessment types inherit from a common style parent.
- **User overrides.** A user-authored theme subtypes the default.
- **Self-visualizing style tree.** The style subgraph is itself renderable by the same pipeline.

---

## Property Representation — [PARTIALLY DEFERRED — ADR-005]

> **v1 reality (Reading A).** Plain RDF triples for property values, and RDF-star where per-value reification is genuinely needed, **are in v1**. The `knm:PropertyDescriptor` class — graph-native definitions of what each property *means*, what types it *applies to*, what data type it *carries* — is in ADR-005's **deferred bucket**. v1 ships without it; property semantics are documented in code/docs, not in the graph. A follow-up ADR will decide whether to promote `PropertyDescriptor` back to substrate-level once the v1 demo exposes the actual pain. The descriptor design below is preserved as the candidate solution for that ADR.

We follow the convergent design pattern of reflexive systems (Smalltalk, Python, MOF-in-practice, RDF/OWL native): **property definitions are graph-native; property values are plain RDF literals; per-value reification is available on demand via RDF-star.**

### The three layers

**1. Property definitions are bubbles.** Every property the system uses has a descriptor node under `knm:`. The descriptor carries what the property means, what values it accepts, what it applies to. Users can inspect, author, and extend these through the graph.

```turtle
knm:color  a knm:PropertyDescriptor ;
    rdfs:label "color" ;
    kn:description "hex color used for rendering" ;
    kn:data_type  xsd:string ;
    kn:applies_to kn:NodeVisualStyle , kn:EdgeVisualStyle .

knm:size  a knm:PropertyDescriptor ;
    rdfs:label "size" ;
    kn:data_type  xsd:integer ;
    kn:applies_to kn:NodeVisualStyle .
```

`knm:PropertyDescriptor` is itself a `kn:NodeType`. Descriptors are ordinary graph data, reachable, renderable, and authorable.

**2. Property values are simple triples.** The actual values stored on domain nodes use the property URI as an ordinary RDF predicate.

```turtle
knm:concept_style  kn:color "#4A90E2" ;
                   kn:size  30 .
```

One triple per fact. No reification. Efficient storage. Standard SPARQL queries work without traversal.

**3. Per-value reification is available on demand** via RDF-star, when a specific value needs metadata (provenance, confidence, authorship):

```turtle
<< knm:concept_style kn:color "#4A90E2" >>
    kn:authored_by knd:prof_smith ;
    kn:created_at "2025-09-15"^^xsd:date ;
    kn:justified_by knd:color_blind_guide .
```

Only the specific statement being annotated pays the reification cost. Unannotated values remain simple triples.

### Why this split

Making every value a reified node breaks performance: on 559 domain nodes with ~5 properties each, full reification costs thousands of extra bubbles the graph has to traverse for every read. Making nothing reifiable breaks reflexivity: the system can't describe its own vocabulary.

Property descriptors at the definition level give the system full self-describing power without paying the reification tax on every data value. RDF-star gives us the escape hatch for cases that genuinely have metadata worth attaching.

### What this gives up

- Users cannot (yet) add new property *kinds* purely through the graph without touching the property descriptor bootstrap. Adding `knm:accessibility_rating` as a new property means adding a descriptor (data) and then using it (more data) — no code change, but there's still a privileged bootstrap step.
- Formal cardinality enforcement (e.g., "a Concept must have exactly one `label`") is not enforced by this structure; it's enforced by validation rules elsewhere (Phase 6).

If these bite in practice, we promote `PropertyDescriptor` to a full `kn:Property` primitive in a future ADR. The migration is mechanical.

---

## Loading Story

On first startup, the C# backend:

1. Checks whether the Jena dataset contains the meta-model (queries for `kn:NodeType a kn:NodeType`).
2. If absent, loads `meta-model.ttl` — a single Turtle file containing the fixed point plus the primitive types and their properties.
3. Loads `meta-instances.ttl` — the authored `knm:*` types (Concept, Principle, prerequisite_of, etc.). These are *data*, not primitives; they live in version control because we ship a default set with the thesis demo, but users can add more.
4. Loads `domain-instances.ttl` — the 559-node curriculum (produced in Stage 3).
5. Runs the projection rule to materialize classical triples.
6. Runs OWL reasoning to derive inferences (prerequisite transitivity, assessment coverage, etc.).
7. Marks `/api/health` as `ready`.

Subsequent startups skip step 2 if the meta-model is already persisted.

---

## Set-Valued Edges (Optional — Metagraph Compatibility)

*Added 2026-04-21 per metagraph discussion. See `RELATED_WORK.md` (parked in `Thesis/Draft 2/`) §"Metagraphs".*

The primitive model defines each `kn:Edge` as having a single `kn:source` and
a single `kn:target`. This covers every binary edge type in the thesis demo.

**Optional extension:** a `kn:Edge` may instead declare `kn:source_set` and/or
`kn:target_set`, pointing to `kn:NodeSet` nodes that enumerate multiple
endpoints. This matches the metagraph formalism of Basu & Blanning (2003),
where an edge is `(A, B)` with A and B subsets of vertices.

```turtle
knd:combined_prereq
    kn:type_of      kn:Edge ;
    kn:type_of      knm:prerequisite_of ;
    kn:source_set   knd:nodeset_algo_trio ;   # MergeSort + Quicksort + HeapSort
    kn:target       knd:Dijkstra .

knd:nodeset_algo_trio
    kn:type_of      kn:NodeSet ;
    kn:members      knd:MergeSort , knd:Quicksort , knd:HeapSort .
```

**Status for thesis demo:** Not used. All demo edges are binary.
**Rendering:** A set-valued edge visualizes as a *combinator node* that fans
out to the set members. Classical-form projection: the edge expands to the
Cartesian product of source and target members (authored edge-type rules
decide which, if any, combinator semantics apply).

This is declared here to keep the door open; the 2003 metagraph work shows
hyperedges are compatible with typed, reified graphs and carry useful
reachability algebra. The demo reserves set-valued edges as future work.

---

## Non-Goals and Deferred Decisions

This document does not cover:

- **Authoring UI for meta-types.** The fact that a user *can* add a new `kn:NodeType` through the same graph API as they add domain nodes is a design constraint, but the concrete authoring UX is a separate ADR.
- **Versioning of meta-types.** If a professor changes `knm:Concept`'s visual style, do we version? Out of scope for Stage 1; tracked as a future decision.
- **Access control.** Who can edit meta-model instances vs. who can edit domain data? Future ADR.
- **Distributed / federated meta-models.** Importing someone else's `knm:*` vocabulary. Conceptually supported by RDF, but no design work yet.
- **Performance optimization of the projection rule.** If the edge count grows, incremental projection beats full rebuild. Deferred until we measure actual performance.

---

Before this document is marked Stage 1 complete, we verify:

- [ ] Every domain type from prior work (9 node types, 13+1+1 edges) is expressible as instances of the primitives defined here. Walk through each explicitly in Stage 2.
- [ ] The fixed-point bootstrap loads into Jena without circularity errors. Tested with a scratch Fuseki instance before Stage 3.
- [ ] OWL reasoning over equivalences produces expected transitive closures on sample data. Sanity check: load 3 prerequisite edges in a chain, verify derived transitive edge appears.
- [ ] SPARQL queries work against both reified and classical forms. `SELECT ?x WHERE { ?x knm:prerequisite_of ?y }` returns results even though the stored form is reified.
- [ ] A proposed domain type change (e.g., "add Misconception as a new NodeType") can be added by writing Turtle, with no code changes in backend or frontend. Confirmed as an integration test in Stage 4.

**Edge types have two faces.** Every `kn:EdgeType` instance simultaneously plays two roles:

1. **As a node.** `knm:prerequisite_of` is a graph node. Users can inspect it, style it, attach descriptions, query its neighborhood, traverse it in the type-view. It has an id, a label, a type (`kn:EdgeType`), and properties.
2. **As a predicate.** `knm:prerequisite_of` is also an RDF property URI. It appears as the predicate in classical triples such as `knd:Variable knm:prerequisite_of knd:Function`. SPARQL patterns and OWL rules operate on it as a relationship, not a node.

Both readings are valid at the same time and on the same URI. RDF permits this because a URI can denote both a resource (node) and a predicate (edge label) without contradiction. This is the structural basis for Level 2 reflexivity: the type system is legible to the engine with the same machinery the domain content uses. A demo that shows the user clicking a `knm:prerequisite_of` node, reading its properties, then running a SPARQL query whose WHERE clause uses that same URI as a predicate, makes the point without any explanation.

## Loading Story

On first startup, the C# backend:

1. Checks whether the Jena dataset contains the meta-model (queries for `kn:NodeType a kn:NodeType`).
2. If absent, loads `meta-model.ttl` — a single Turtle file containing the fixed point plus the primitive types and their properties.
3. Loads `meta-instances.ttl` — the authored `knm:*` types (Concept, Principle, prerequisite_of, etc.). These are *data*, not primitives; they live in version control because we ship a default set with the thesis demo, but users can add more.
4. Loads `domain-instances.ttl` — the 559-node curriculum (produced in Stage 3).
5. Runs the projection rule to materialize classical triples.
6. Runs OWL reasoning to derive inferences (prerequisite transitivity, assessment coverage, etc.).
7. Marks `/api/health` as `ready`.

Subsequent startups skip step 2 if the meta-model is already persisted.

## Loading Story

On first startup, the C# backend:

1. Checks whether the Jena dataset contains the meta-model (queries for `kn:NodeType kn:type_of kn:NodeType`).
2. If absent, loads `meta.ttl` — the kernel: 14 `kn:*` symbols (4 node-type primitives, 4 edge-type primitives, 3 reflexivity-rendering, 3 inference-protocol).

## Set-Valued Edges (Optional — Metagraph Compatibility)

*Added 2026-04-21 per metagraph discussion. See `RELATED_WORK.md` (parked in `Thesis/Draft 2/`) §"Metagraphs".*

The primitive model defines each `kn:Edge` as having a single `kn:source` and
a single `kn:target`. This covers every binary edge type in the thesis demo.

**Optional extension:** a `kn:Edge` may instead declare `kn:source_set` and/or
`kn:target_set`, pointing to `kn:NodeSet` nodes that enumerate multiple
endpoints. This matches the metagraph formalism of Basu & Blanning (2003),
where an edge is `(A, B)` with A and B subsets of vertices.

```turtle
knd:combined_prereq
    kn:type_of      kn:Edge ;
    kn:type_of      knm:prerequisite_of ;
    kn:source_set   knd:nodeset_algo_trio ;   # MergeSort + Quicksort + HeapSort
    kn:target       knd:Dijkstra .

knd:nodeset_algo_trio
    kn:type_of      kn:NodeSet ;
    kn:members      knd:MergeSort , knd:Quicksort , knd:HeapSort .
```

**Status for thesis demo:** Not used. All demo edges are binary.
**Rendering:** A set-valued edge visualizes as a *combinator node* that fans
out to the set members. Classical-form projection: the edge expands to the
Cartesian product of source and target members (authored edge-type rules
decide which, if any, combinator semantics apply).

This is declared here to keep the door open; the 2003 metagraph work shows
hyperedges are compatible with typed, reified graphs and carry useful
reachability algebra. The demo reserves set-valued edges as future work.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The `meta-instances.ttl` reference in Loading Story stayed deliberately abstract. Pre-addendum it had a fixed name; post-addendum the file structure depends on reclassification (`knl:*` edge types vs. user-namespace types), which hasn't been done yet. So the doc now describes *what* gets loaded, not *which file* — the file-naming decision migrates with the reclassification work.
- Provenance/timestamp swap (`prov:wasAttributedTo`, `dcterms:created`) is more than cosmetic: it makes the demo's reified-edge metadata directly compatible with PROV-O tooling that ADR-007's pipeline already uses for `prov:wasGeneratedBy` markers. One vocabulary across substrate annotations and pipeline output.
- The "Set-Valued Edges" downgrade from "Optional" to "[DEFERRED]" matters for the thesis claim count: if we keep waving at metagraph compatibility as if it's wired, defenders pick at it. Marking it deferred-bucket aligns the doc with what's actually buildable in v1.

content.content:
1	# Type-View Edge Scope Specification
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	**Date:** 2026-04-28
5	**Related:** ADR-003 (reflexivity foundation), ADR-005 (`kn:` scope under Reading A; deferred-bucket resolutions), ADR-006 (node-as-document binding), VISION.md §4.8 (reflexive substrate), Claim 7
6	**Implements:** Step 8 of the post-Stage-5 reconciliation
7	**Audience:** Backend (SPARQL query authors, `SparqlGraphRepository` maintainers); frontend (graph-store consumers); thesis defense (Claim 7 evidence).
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Purpose
12	
13	Stage 5 ships `/api/graph?view=type` as a live demonstration of Claim 7 (the substrate meta-model is held in the same RDF graph as user content and renders through the same engine). This document specifies, exactly, **what RDF triples are projected as type-view nodes and edges** so that:
14	
15	1. The Stage 5 SPARQL queries (`nodes-meta.rq`, `edges-meta.rq`) are unambiguously aligned with the post-reconciliation substrate (`kn:` reduced to 14 symbols per ADR-005's deferred-bucket resolutions).
16	2. Future substrate changes have a single place to update the projection contract.
17	3. Thesis defense has a precise spec to point at when explaining what the type-view shows.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 1. Inputs
22	
23	The type-view projects against the live Fuseki triple store. Three kinds of triples are relevant:
24	
25	- **Substrate triples** (`meta.ttl`): the 14-symbol `kn:` kernel and its self-typing fixed point.
26	- **Meta-instance triples** (`knl:`): engine-required edge types referenced by name in engine code (5–7 symbols per ADR-005 addendum).
27	- **User-namespace meta-instance triples** (e.g., `cs:`): NodeTypes and EdgeTypes the user authors for their domain.
28	
29	User-content triples (M0 — domain instances like `cs:variable`) are **not** part of the type-view. They are rendered by `view=knowledge`, which is out of scope for this spec.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. Type-View Nodes
34	
35	### 2.1 Inclusion set
36	
37	A node `n` belongs to the type-view if and only if at least one of the following holds:
38	
39	| Condition | Examples |
40	|---|---|
41	| `n` is one of the four L1 primitives | `kn:Node`, `kn:Edge`, `kn:NodeType`, `kn:EdgeType` |
42	| `n` has `n a kn:NodeType` (or equivalently `n kn:type_of kn:NodeType`) | `knl:prerequisite_of` is *not* matched here (it's an EdgeType); `cs:Course` is matched |
43	| `n` has `n a kn:EdgeType` (or equivalently `n kn:type_of kn:EdgeType`) | `knl:prerequisite_of`, `knl:demonstrates`, `cs:teaches` |
44	
45	The L1 primitives are included explicitly via a `VALUES` clause because their self-typing uses `kn:type_of` rather than `rdf:type`. (See `meta.ttl`: `kn:NodeType kn:type_of kn:NodeType` is the fixed point.)
46	
47	### 2.2 Explicit exclusions
48	
49	The type-view never contains:
50	
51	- **Reified edge instances** (`?e a kn:Edge` style nodes). These are M0 — domain edges materialized as nodes for property-bearing. They render in `view=knowledge`, not the type-view.
52	- **User-content M0 nodes** (`cs:variable`, `cs:turing_test`, etc.). Domain instances render in `view=knowledge`.
53	- **Document-body URIs** (`urn:knd-body:*` opaque URNs from ADR-006). These are SQLite doc-store identifiers, not RDF nodes; they never appear as graph nodes.
54	- **Visual-style class nodes and instances** (any `kn:VisualStyle` / `kn:NodeVisualStyle` / `kn:EdgeVisualStyle` lineage). Per ADR-005 these have left the graph entirely.
55	- **Reference-ontology nodes** (`cso:*`, `skos:Concept`, `schema:Course`, etc.) when imported as named graphs. These are background vocabulary, not type-view content.
56	
57	  *Exception note:* a user-authored NodeType that explicitly declares `owl:equivalentClass skos:Concept` is still a type-view node (because it's typed as `kn:NodeType` in the user's named graph). The reference-ontology side of the equivalence is not pulled in.
58	
59	### 2.3 Node properties (rendered as property bag, not edges)
60	
61	For each type-view node `n`, the following triples are projected as **node properties** (not edges) on the wire:
62	
63	| Predicate | Source | Wire form |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| `rdfs:label` | substrate / user | string |
66	| `rdfs:comment` | substrate / user | string (replaces `kn:description` per ADR-005 deferred-bucket resolution) |
67	| `kn:edge_category` | substrate (on EdgeType nodes) | string literal: `"system"` or `"domain"` |
68	| `kn:owl_semantics` | substrate (on EdgeType nodes) | IRI: `owl:TransitiveProperty`, `owl:SymmetricProperty`, `owl:FunctionalProperty`, `owl:InverseFunctionalProperty` (one or more) |
69	| `kn:derived` | substrate (on EdgeType nodes) | boolean |
70	| `owl:equivalentClass`, `owl:equivalentProperty` | substrate / user | IRI of the aligned class/property; rendered as a property, not as a graph edge |
71	
72	These are properties because they describe a single node's metadata. They are not edges between type-view nodes.
73	
74	---
75	
76	## 3. Type-View Edges
77	
78	### 3.1 Inclusion rule
79	
80	A triple `(s, p, o)` is projected as a type-view edge if and only if **all three** of:
81	
82	1. `s` is a type-view node (per §2).
83	2. `o` is a type-view node (per §2).
84	3. `p` is one of the projection predicates listed in §3.2.
85	
86	### 3.2 Projection predicates
87	
88	The five predicates that project as edges in the type-view:
89	
90	| Predicate | Direction | Endpoint constraint | Rationale |
91	|---|---|---|---|
92	| `kn:type_of` | instance → type | both endpoints are type-view nodes | The primary meta-relation. Includes the fixed point `kn:NodeType kn:type_of kn:NodeType`. |
93	| `kn:subtype_of` | subtype → supertype | NodeType→NodeType *or* EdgeType→EdgeType | Generalization between types. |
94	| `rdfs:domain` | EdgeType → NodeType | source is `a kn:EdgeType`; target is a NodeType | Source-role constraint on edges. Replaces `kn:domain` per ADR-005 deferred-bucket resolution. |
95	| `rdfs:range` | EdgeType → NodeType | source is `a kn:EdgeType`; target is a NodeType | Target-role constraint on edges. Replaces `kn:range` per ADR-005 deferred-bucket resolution. |
96	| `kn:inverse_edge_type` | EdgeType → EdgeType | both endpoints are EdgeTypes | Visualizes inverse pairing for inference (e.g., `knl:demonstrates ↔ knl:is_demonstrated_by`). |
97	
98	### 3.3 Explicit exclusions
99	
100	The type-view never projects edges for:
101	
102	- **`kn:source` / `kn:target`** — these belong to reified `kn:Edge` instances at M0 level, not the meta-model. They render in `view=knowledge` after the M0-projection SPARQL CONSTRUCT.
103	- **`kn:edge_category`, `kn:owl_semantics`, `kn:derived`** — these are *node properties* per §2.3, not edges. They describe the EdgeType node, not relationships between nodes.
104	- **`rdfs:label` / `rdfs:comment`** — node properties, not edges.
105	- **`owl:equivalentClass` / `owl:equivalentProperty`** — node properties (identity assertions), not graph edges. (Future revision may project these as a distinct edge category if the type-view needs to render external-ontology alignments per ADR-007.)
106	- **`kn:contains`** — reflexivity-rendering vocab from ADR-005, but in v1 it is used only at M0 (sub-document containment per ADR-006), not between NodeTypes. Excluded by default. *Re-include if a future change introduces NodeType-level containment.*
107	- **`kn:body_ref`** — points from M0 nodes to opaque doc-store URNs. Never appears in the type-view.
108	
109	### 3.4 Edge identity synthesis
110	
111	Type-view edges are not stored. They are synthesized at query time. Each projected triple gets a stable, deterministic edge ID under the synthesized `kne:` namespace:
112	
113	```
114	kne:{source-local}--{predicate-local}--{target-local}
115	```
116	
117	where `{*-local}` is the trailing local name of the corresponding URI (everything after the last `#` or `/`).
118	
119	The `kne:` namespace exists only on the wire and only for type-view edges. It is not authored and never appears as a stored triple.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## 4. Self-Loops and the Fixed Point
124	
125	The substrate's self-typing fixed point is **always** present in the type-view as a self-loop edge:
126	
127	```
128	kn:NodeType --kn:type_of--> kn:NodeType
129	```
130	
131	This is intentional. Claim 7 rests on the visible self-reference. The frontend renders this as a loop edge on the `kn:NodeType` node.
132	
133	Other potential self-loops (e.g., a hypothetical `kn:Node kn:subtype_of kn:Node`) do not exist in the substrate; primitives do not subtype themselves.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 5. Excluded by Construction (Why the Spec Stays Small)
138	
139	Several categories of triples that *could* exist in the graph are deliberately excluded from the type-view. Recording them here so future change-makers know not to add them back without an ADR:
140	
141	- **Reified edge instances** (`?e a kn:Edge`): M0 content. Render in `view=knowledge` via the SPARQL CONSTRUCT projection rule.
142	- **PROV-O provenance triples** added by the EVōC + CSO pipeline (per ADR-007): describe minted M0 concepts. Not type-view material.
143	- **SHACL shapes** (per ADR-005 deferred-bucket resolution for `sh:in`): may exist in the graph if `kn:allowed_values` audit replaces with SHACL. Not projected — shapes describe constraints, which the type-view does not render in v1.
144	- **External reference ontologies** (CSO, SKOS core, schema.org) when loaded as named graphs: background context, not type-view nodes.
145	
146	If any of these need to render in the type-view in a future version, that is an explicit spec change requiring an ADR (or this document's revision).
147	
148	---
149	
150	## 6. Wire Output Shape
151	
152	The `/api/graph?view=type` endpoint returns the same `GraphEnvelope` DTO as `view=knowledge`. The output is a uniform graph shape regardless of view, which is what makes Claim 7's "rendered by the same engine" claim concrete.
153	
154	```jsonc
155	{
156	  "nodes": [
157	    {
158	      "id":    "<URI of type-view node>",
159	      "type":  "<URI of kn:NodeType or kn:EdgeType>",
160	      "label": "<rdfs:label>",
161	      "properties": {
162	        "<predicateURI>": <jsonValue>,
163	        ...
164	      }
165	    },
166	    ...
167	  ],
168	  "edges": [
169	    {
170	      "id":     "<synthesized kne: URI>",
171	      "type":   "<projection predicate URI: kn:type_of, kn:subtype_of, rdfs:domain, rdfs:range, or kn:inverse_edge_type>",
172	      "source": "<URI of source type-view node>",
173	      "target": "<URI of target type-view node>"
174	    },
175	    ...
176	  ]
177	}
178	```
179	
180	---
181	
182	## 7. Migration Tasks
183	
184	These align with the post-Stage-5 reconciliation Step 10 (`meta.ttl` audit) and follow directly from this spec:
185	
186	1. **Update `nodes-meta.rq`:** no change required (current logic already matches §2). Verify after the `meta.ttl` audit removes visual-style nodes.
187	2. **Update `edges-meta.rq`:** replace `kn:domain` / `kn:range` in the `VALUES ?type` clause with `rdfs:domain` / `rdfs:range`. Add `kn:type_of` and `kn:inverse_edge_type` to the projected predicate set.

190	
191	---
192	
193	## 8. Acceptance Criteria
194	
195	The type-view spec is correctly implemented when:
196	
197	1. `/api/graph?view=type` returns a node for every URI typed as `kn:NodeType` or `kn:EdgeType`, plus the four L1 primitives.
198	2. Every returned edge has a predicate in `{kn:type_of, kn:subtype_of, rdfs:domain, rdfs:range, kn:inverse_edge_type}`.
199	3. The fixed-point self-loop `kn:NodeType --kn:type_of--> kn:NodeType` is present in the edge list.
