# Knowledge Node Model

**Status:** Rewritten 2026-04-21 to align with [ADR-003](ADR-003-reflexivity-as-foundation.md) and [META_MODEL_DESIGN.md](META_MODEL_DESIGN.md)
**Scope:** Domain-layer node model. Specifies what a user-authored knowledge node looks like on top of the reflexive meta-model.
**Deciders:** Shizhong Yu

> **Before reading this doc, read [META_MODEL_DESIGN.md](META_MODEL_DESIGN.md).**
> That document defines the four primitive node types (`kn:Node`, `kn:NodeType`,
> `kn:EdgeType`, `kn:Edge`) and the bootstrap graph. This document describes the
> *domain layer* that sits on top of that foundation.

---

## Relationship to the Meta-Model

The meta-model (Level 1 / `kn:*`) defines what a node is. This document
describes how *domain* nodes — the things a professor actually authors,
like "Merge Sort" or "Stability" — fit into that structure.

```
Level 1 (meta)       : kn:Node, kn:NodeType, kn:EdgeType, kn:Edge          (in META_MODEL_DESIGN.md)
Level 2 (meta-inst.) : knm:Concept, knm:Principle, knm:prerequisite_of…    (in TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md)
Level 3 (domain)     : knd:MergeSort, knd:Stability, knd:edge_0042…        (this document)
```

**A domain node is an `rdf:type` (equivalently `kn:type_of`) instance of a
meta-instance node type.** The meta-instance node type is itself a node of
type `kn:NodeType`, which is itself a node of type `kn:NodeType` (the fixed
point). Three levels, one graph.

---

## Core Principle: Everything Is a Node

Every entity in the system — knowledge items, types, edges, edge types,
visual styles, property descriptors, artifacts — is a `kn:Node`. Structure
lives in edges, not in nested data structures.

Consequences:

- Types (e.g., `knm:Concept`) are nodes — they can be queried, annotated,
  versioned, and styled.
- Edges (e.g., "Merge Sort is a prerequisite of Quicksort") have
  identity — each is a `kn:Edge` node with `kn:source`, `kn:target`, and
  `kn:type_of` references. Annotations like authorship and confidence attach
  to the edge node.
- Edge types (e.g., `knm:prerequisite_of`) are nodes — they can declare OWL
  characteristics, visual styles, and category membership.

This is the reflexivity commitment. See [ADR-003](ADR-003-reflexivity-as-foundation.md).

---

## Hierarchy Is Computed, Not Stored

A knowledge node does **not** store a `parentId` or `childrenIds`.
Parent/child relationships are always **derived** from context:

| Context | How hierarchy is computed |
|---|---|
| Explicit authoring | Domain edges (`knm:generalizes`, `knm:is_component_of`) |
| Lifecycle / ownership | System edges (`knm:sys_contains`) |
| Semantic similarity | Word embeddings → EVōC clustering |
| Traversal intent | Active strategy (Linear, Explore, Problem-First) |
| Complexity level | Node-type filter (Level 1–4 in the demo) |

**Hierarchy is a view.** The same node can appear as a child in one context
and a parent in another.

---

## Domain Node Shape

A domain node is an RDF resource with the following shape. Only the first
three are mandatory; everything else is optional.

| Property | RDF | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| identity | URI (`knd:…`) | Globally-unique resource identifier |
| type | `kn:type_of` → `knm:<NodeType>` | What kind of thing it is |
| label | `rdfs:label` (literal) | Human-readable name |
| description | `kn:description` (literal) | Content — also the embedding source |
| external document | `kn:document_id` (literal) | Stub link to external block-editor doc |
| artifacts | `kn:has_artifact` → artifact node(s) | File attachments (see "Artifacts") |

Turtle example:

```turtle
knd:MergeSort
    a                    knm:Concept ;
    rdfs:label           "Merge Sort" ;
    kn:description       "Divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm with O(n log n) time."@en ;
    kn:document_id       "doc_ms_001" .
```

Type-specific extra properties (e.g., `kn:course_code` on Course nodes, `kn:format`
on Assessment nodes) are defined as `knm:PropertyDescriptor` nodes per
META_MODEL_DESIGN §"Property Representation". See TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md for the
full catalog of domain property descriptors.

---

## Edges in the Domain

Every authored edge is a `kn:Edge` node. Reified form is the canonical
storage; classical form is derived by SPARQL CONSTRUCT at load time (see
META_MODEL_DESIGN §"Dual-form edges"). Authors and UIs interact with
classical form for simplicity; the reified form is available for annotation.

Turtle example (reified):

```turtle
knd:edge_0042
    a                    kn:Edge ;
    kn:type_of           knm:prerequisite_of ;
    kn:source            knd:MergeSort ;
    kn:target            knd:Quicksort ;
    kn:authored_by       knd:ProfChen ;
    kn:created_at        "2026-03-15T09:22Z"^^xsd:dateTime .
```

Classical form (derived):

```turtle
knd:MergeSort knm:prerequisite_of knd:Quicksort .
```

Both coexist in the store.

---

## System vs Domain Edges

The conceptual distinction from [ADR-002](ADR-002-system-vs-domain-namespace.md)
still holds: **system edges manage lifecycle**, **domain edges carry meaning**.

With reflexivity, the distinction is no longer a URI prefix. Every edge type
is a `kn:EdgeType` node carrying an `kn:edge_category` property:

| `kn:edge_category` | Examples | Owner | UI visibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"system"` | `knm:sys_contains` | Engine/developer | Hidden by default, power-user toggle |
| `"domain"` | `knm:prerequisite_of`, `knm:contains`, `knm:teaches` | Professor | Always visible |

Both categories can coexist on the same node pair. A node might have both
`knm:sys_contains` (lifecycle binding) and `knm:is_component_of` (semantic
part-of) pointing at it from the same owner — these are independent axes.

See TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md for the full edge-type catalog with categories.

---

## `knm:sys_contains` — Lifecycle Ownership

The only system edge in scope for the thesis demo. Defines subnode ownership:
the structural relationship where one node's lifecycle is bound to another.

Behavioral properties live on the *edge instance* as property triples:

| Property | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `kn:on_delete` | `"cascade"`, `"detach"`, `"prevent"` | Action when owner is deleted |
| `kn:exclusive` | `true` / `false` | Can target have ≥2 ownership edges? |
| `kn:auto_created` | `true` / `false` | Did the tool create this? |
| `kn:user_editable` | `true` / `false` | Can the user modify? |

Default instance for `knm:sys_contains`: `cascade`, `exclusive=true`,
`user_editable=false`.

### Exclusivity rule

A node can be the target of at most one `knm:sys_contains` edge. To share,
detach first.

### SQL parallel

| Graph concept | SQL equivalent |
|---|---|
| `knm:sys_contains` (exclusive) | Identifying relationship |
| `on_delete "cascade"` | `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `on_delete "detach"` | `ON DELETE SET NULL` |
| `on_delete "prevent"` | `ON DELETE RESTRICT` |

---

## Decision Guide: `knm:sys_contains` vs `knm:is_component_of`

| Criterion | `knm:sys_contains` (system) | `knm:is_component_of` (domain) |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Lifecycle ownership | Semantic part-whole meaning |
| Axis | Structural | Semantic |
| Delete behavior | Cascade/detach/prevent | None — independent existence |
| Exclusivity | One owner only | Many-to-many |
| Auto-created | Yes (by tool actions) | No (explicitly authored) |
| UI visibility | Hidden by default | Always visible |
| Example | `Bubble Sort knm:sys_contains "Implement Bubble Sort"` | `Divide and Conquer knm:is_component_of Merge Sort` |

**Use `knm:sys_contains`** when the child was created FOR the parent — its
content only makes sense in the parent's context; cascade on delete.

**Use `knm:is_component_of`** when the child is a conceptually independent
idea that happens to be part of the parent.

**Use both** when a node is both structurally owned and conceptually a part
of the parent.

---

## Promotion

Block-based editors allow "promoting" a content section into its own node.
The thesis demo does not implement the promotion UI, but the model supports it:

Promotion creates a new node + **two edges**:

1. **`knm:sys_contains` edge** (tool-authored) — lifecycle ownership.
   `auto_created=true`, `exclusive=true`, `on_delete="cascade"`.
2. **Domain semantic edge** (author-supplied) — the author picks
   `knm:is_component_of`, `knm:applies_in`, or similar. Anchors the new
   node's semantic identity.

Example: promoting "Implement Bubble Sort" from within the Bubble Sort content:

- Tool creates: `BubbleSort knm:sys_contains "Implement Bubble Sort"` (lifecycle)
- Author creates: `"Implement Bubble Sort" knm:applies_in BubbleSort` (semantic)

**Thesis demo scope:** Promotion UI is not implemented. The 559 nodes are
hand-authored; edge choices reflect what promotion would have produced.

---

## Artifacts

File attachments (PDFs, images, code files). The pragmatic shape for the
thesis demo keeps artifact data inline with the parent node:

```turtle
knd:MergeSort
    a                knm:Concept ;
    rdfs:label       "Merge Sort" ;
    kn:has_artifact  knd:artifact_ms_01 ,
                     knd:artifact_ms_02 .

knd:artifact_ms_01
    a                knm:Artifact ;
    kn:file_path     "resources/ms/clrs-ch2-3.pdf" ;
    kn:mime_type     "application/pdf" ;
    rdfs:label       "CLRS Chapter 2.3" .
```

Artifacts are `knm:Artifact` nodes (declared in TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN), so the
"everything is a node" rule holds without special-casing. The 559 demo nodes
have no artifact data; this schema is future-ready.

---

## Domain Specialization: 6-Course CS Program

The thesis demo is a specialization of the base schema for a 6-course CS
undergraduate program knowledge graph, used as a professor-facing course
management and authoring tool.

- **Primary user:** Professor — authors the graph, validates structure, inspects learning paths
- **Scale:** 559 nodes across 6 courses (CS101–CS402) with 22 shared cross-course principles
- **Node type count:** 9 (6 knowledge types + 3 organizational types)
- **Edge type count:** 14 (13 domain + 1 system) + 1 derived (`knm:assesses`)

Full type catalog: [TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md](phase-2-type-system/TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md).

### Multi-Course Containment

```
Program
├── knm:sys_contains → Course (×6)
├── knm:sys_contains → Professor (×3)
└── each Course
    └── knm:sys_contains → knowledge nodes (Concepts, Examples, Assessments, References, Analogies)
        └── some Concepts → knm:sys_contains → sub-concepts
```

Shared Principles (22) are NOT contained by any course — they connect via
`knm:demonstrates` domain edges across courses.

### Hierarchy in the Education Domain

| View/Context | How hierarchy is computed |
|---|---|
| Level 1–4 complexity filter | Node-type inclusion rules (Concept+Principle → +Example → +Assessment:exercise → all six) |
| Compound graph nesting | `knm:generalizes` and `knm:is_component_of` edges define visual containment |
| Linear traversal | Follow `knm:prerequisite_of` chain from a start Concept |
| Explore traversal | All domain edge types from a selected node |
| Problem-First traversal | Backward reachability over `knm:prerequisite_of` from an Assessment |
| EVōC cluster view | Computed from `kn:description` embeddings (primary layout) |

---

## Implications for the Frontend (`types.ts`)

The frontend still renders typed data — React components need TypeScript
interfaces. These are **derived views** of the RDF store: SPARQL results
projected into typed objects. They are *not* the source of truth.

The frontend types mirror the classical (projected) form of the graph:

```typescript
interface KnowledgeNode {
  id: string                  // URI or local identifier
  label: string               // rdfs:label
  type: string                // URI of the knm:NodeType
  description?: string        // kn:description
  documentId?: string         // kn:document_id
  artifacts: Artifact[]       // resolved from kn:has_artifact
}

interface KnowledgeEdge {
  id: string                  // URI of the kn:Edge node (reified form)
  source: string              // source node URI
  target: string              // target node URI
  type: string                // URI of the knm:EdgeType
  category: 'system' | 'domain'   // from the edge type's kn:edge_category
  inferred?: boolean          // true = derived by Jena
  properties?: Record<string, unknown>   // per-edge properties (e.g., on_delete)
}
```

The backend is responsible for producing these shapes from SPARQL queries.
See the backend API spec in THESIS_DEMO_GAP_ANALYSIS.md.

---

## Resolved Decisions (Historical)

### Session 1 (2026-04-10)

| Question | Resolution |
|---|---|
| How do `Stability` and `In-Place Sorting` principles connect to sort concepts? | **`demonstrates` edge** — Concept → Principle; inverse `is_demonstrated_by` |
| How do Exercise nodes connect? | **Exercise merged into Assessment** — `format: 'exercise'`; same `applies_in` connection |
| EVōC embedding source | **Deferred** until rest of system is built |

### Session 2 (2026-04-11)

| Question | Resolution |
|---|---|
| How are subnodes distinguished from peer nodes? | **`sys:contains` system edge** — lifecycle ownership with behavioral properties |
| Should system and domain edges share a schema? | **Orthogonal axes** — both coexist on same node pairs |
| Edge naming convention | **Colon-separated qualified names** (later replaced by `kn:edge_category` property in ADR-003) |
| Subnode exclusivity | **One owner** via `sys:contains`; sharing requires promotion to independent node first |
| System edge visual treatment | **Muted/dotted/toggle-able** |
| Artifacts as nodes | **Adopted** in the rewrite — `knm:Artifact` is a node type |

### Session 3 (2026-04-11)

| Question | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Demo domain | **Python 101** — replaced sorting algorithms |
| Primary user persona | **Professor as course author** |
| Org layer (students, TAs, departments) | **Deferred** |

### Session 5 (2026-04-16)

| Question | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Scale expansion | **26 → 559 nodes** across 6 courses |
| Organizational node types | **3 new types: Program, Course, Professor** — always visible |
| `teaches` edge | **Domain edge** — Professor → Course (ADR-002) |
| Assessment format | **`'test' \| 'exercise' \| 'quiz'`** — dropped `'exam'` |
| Shared principles | **22 principles NOT contained by courses** — cross-cutting |

### Reflexivity Pivot (2026-04-20, ADR-003)

| Question | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Storage layer | Neo4j removed. Apache Jena Fuseki is primary. |
| Node model | Reflexive — types, edge types, edges are all nodes. |
| Edge representation | Reified (canonical) + classical (derived). Both coexist. |
| Namespace encoding | `sys:`/`domain:` prefix → `kn:edge_category` property on edge-type nodes. |
| Frontend types | Remain as derived view; backend projects SPARQL results into them. |

---

## Open Items

- Artifact node URIs: currently `knd:artifact_*`. A dedicated `kna:` namespace
  may be introduced if artifact management scales.
- Property descriptors for type-specific fields (`format`, `url`, `course_code`,
  `department`) are cataloged in TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.
- Edge instance property schema (`kn:on_delete`, `kn:exclusive`, etc.) may
  move to a dedicated SYSTEM_EDGE_SCHEMA doc if it grows.

| Context | How hierarchy is computed |

| Explicit authoring | Domain edges (`knm:generalizes`, `knm:is_component_of`) |

## `knm:sys_contains` — Lifecycle Ownership

The only system edge in scope for the thesis demo. Defines subnode ownership:
the structural relationship where one node's lifecycle is bound to another.

Behavioral properties live on the *edge instance* as property triples:

| Property | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `kn:on_delete` | `"cascade"`, `"detach"`, `"prevent"` | Action when owner is deleted |
| `kn:exclusive` | `true` / `false` | Can target have ≥2 ownership edges? |
| `kn:auto_created` | `true` / `false` | Did the tool create this? |
| `kn:user_editable` | `true` / `false` | Can the user modify? |

Default instance for `knm:sys_contains`: `cascade`, `exclusive=true`,
`user_editable=false`.

### Exclusivity rule

A node can be the target of at most one `knm:sys_contains` edge. To share,
detach first.

### SQL parallel

| Graph concept | SQL equivalent |
|---|---|
| `knm:sys_contains` (exclusive) | Identifying relationship |
| `on_delete "cascade"` | `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `on_delete "detach"` | `ON DELETE SET NULL` |
| `on_delete "prevent"` | `ON DELETE RESTRICT` |

## `kn:contains` — Lifecycle Ownership (Kernel Symbol)

The kernel structural parent-child edge from ADR-006. Defines subnode
ownership: the relationship where one node's lifecycle is bound to another
through document-internal containment (block → child node) or organizational
binding.

> **Naming history.** Pre-2026-04-28 this was called `knm:sys_contains` and
> was authored at meta-instance level. ADR-006 promoted it to a kernel symbol
> (`kn:contains`) as part of the node-as-document binding decision. The
> demo-curriculum organizational containment (Course → Concept) lives at a

> **Reading A status.** Per ADR-005, lifecycle behavioral properties
> (`kn:on_delete`, `kn:exclusive`, `kn:auto_created`, `kn:user_editable`)
> are **not** in the v1 graph. They are app-config or code constants
> attached to the kernel `kn:contains` semantics. The design below is
> preserved as candidate Reading B/C content if lifecycle properties are
> later promoted to graph-native data.

Candidate per-edge-instance properties (deferred):

| Property | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| (deferred) on-delete | `"cascade"`, `"detach"`, `"prevent"` | Action when owner is deleted |
| (deferred) exclusive | `true` / `false` | Can target have ≥2 ownership edges? |
| (deferred) auto-created | `true` / `false` | Did the tool create this? |
| (deferred) user-editable | `true` / `false` | Can the user modify? |

`user_editable=false`.

### Exclusivity rule

A node can be the target of at most one `kn:contains` edge. To share,
detach first. Enforced in app code in v1; SHACL shape is the candidate
graph-native enforcement mechanism.

## Decision Guide: `knm:sys_contains` vs `knm:is_component_of`

| Criterion | `knm:sys_contains` (system) | `knm:is_component_of` (domain) |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Lifecycle ownership | Semantic part-whole meaning |
| Axis | Structural | Semantic |
| Delete behavior | Cascade/detach/prevent | None — independent existence |
| Exclusivity | One owner only | Many-to-many |
| Auto-created | Yes (by tool actions) | No (explicitly authored) |
| UI visibility | Hidden by default | Always visible |
| Example | `Bubble Sort knm:sys_contains "Implement Bubble Sort"` | `Divide and Conquer knm:is_component_of Merge Sort` |

**Use `knm:sys_contains`** when the child was created FOR the parent — its
content only makes sense in the parent's context; cascade on delete.

**Use `knm:is_component_of`** when the child is a conceptually independent
idea that happens to be part of the parent.

**Use both** when a node is both structurally owned and conceptually a part
of the parent.

## Artifacts — superseded by ADR-006

> **Status (2026-04-28).** The pre-addendum design treated file attachments
> as `knm:Artifact` graph nodes linked via `kn:has_artifact`. ADR-006 supersedes
> this: document body content is bound via the kernel symbol `kn:body_ref`
> to an opaque doc-store URN, and file attachments are managed by the
> SQLite doc store (or equivalent) — they are not RDF nodes in v1.

```turtle
cs:MergeSort
    a                cs:Concept ;
    rdfs:label       "Merge Sort" ;
    rdfs:comment     "Divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm with O(n log n) time." ;
    kn:body_ref      <urn:knd-body:ms-001> .
```

The doc-store URN resolves to a structured document (block-editor format)
that may contain file references, but those references are not graph nodes.
This collapses two prior predicates (`kn:document_id` for the body link,
`kn:has_artifact` for attachments) into the single kernel symbol
`kn:body_ref`.

The `knm:Artifact` node type is removed from the v1 catalog (see
TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN §1).

### Reflexivity Pivot (2026-04-20, ADR-003)

| Question | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Storage layer | Neo4j removed. Apache Jena Fuseki is primary. |
| Node model | Reflexive — types, edge types, edges are all nodes. |
| Edge representation | Reified (canonical) + classical (derived). Both coexist. |
| Namespace encoding | `sys:`/`domain:` prefix → `kn:edge_category` property on edge-type nodes. |
| Frontend types | Remain as derived view; backend projects SPARQL results into them. |

### Namespace Addendum + Deferred-Bucket Resolutions (2026-04-28, ADR-005)

| Question | Resolution |
|---|---|
| `kn:` kernel size | Locked at 14 symbols (8 bootstrap + 3 reflexivity-rendering + 3 inference protocol). |
| `knm:` namespace | Renamed to `knl:` (engine standard library); narrowed to engine-required edges (~5 symbols) per engine-feature test. |
| Education-specific types (`Concept`, `Course`, `Professor`, etc.) | Moved to demo's user namespace `cs:`. Engine ships no node-type catalog. |
| `knd:` (domain instances) | Replaced by user namespace `cs:` — both types and instances live there. |
| `kn:description` / `kn:domain` / `kn:range` / `kn:data_type` | Replaced by W3C standards `rdfs:comment` / `rdfs:domain` / `rdfs:range` / `xsd:*` typed literals. |

KNOWLEDGE_NODE_MODEL clean — all hits are deliberate "renamed from X" / "replaces X" / historical-log references. Phase 4 done.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Lifecycle properties (`on_delete`, `exclusive`, `auto_created`, `user_editable`) leaving the graph is the most consequential v1 simplification in this doc. The pre-addendum design had lifecycle metadata as graph-native triples — meaning every cascade decision was queryable and overridable. v1 collapses to "kernel `kn:contains` semantics, app-config defaults" — simpler, but loses the demo-as-data property for lifecycle. Worth flagging on thesis defense if a panelist asks.
- The "Resolved Decisions (Historical)" section gained a 5th entry (2026-04-28 ADR-005 addendum). Keeping the chronology lets a reader trace WHY a decision is what it is, not just what it is. ADR-style log of "we changed from X to Y because Z" is more defensible than just "Y is what we have."
- `kn:contains` doing double duty (kernel structural per ADR-006 + lifecycle ownership for the demo) is fine because semantically they're the same relation — "X structurally owns Y, lifecycle bound." The old `knm:sys_contains` was just naming the same thing at meta-instance level. Promoting it to kernel cuts a layer without adding semantics.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

# ADR-002: System vs Domain Namespace Architecture

**Status:** Accepted — mechanism amended by [ADR-003](ADR-003-reflexivity-as-foundation.md) (2026-04-20)
**Date:** 2026-04-16
**Deciders:** Shizhong Yu
**Context area:** Cross-cutting — affects edge schema, data model, all subsystems

---

## ⚠️ Amendment — 2026-04-20 (ADR-003 Reflexivity Pivot)

**The conceptual separation still holds.** System edges (lifecycle, cascade,
exclusivity) and domain edges (user-authored knowledge relationships) remain
architecturally distinct, for the same reasons: different owners, different
invariants, different change frequencies.

**The mechanism has changed.** The distinction is no longer encoded as a URI
namespace prefix (`sys:` vs. unprefixed). Instead:

- Every edge type is a `kn:EdgeType` node in the graph.
- System-level edge types (e.g., `knm:sys_contains`) carry an
  `kn:edge_category` property with value `"system"`.
- Domain-level edge types (e.g., `knm:prerequisite_of`, `knm:contains`) carry
  `kn:edge_category "domain"`.
- Subsystems query the edge-type node to determine category, rather than
  pattern-matching URI prefixes.

**Why the change:** Reflexivity means edge types are graph-native nodes with
their own properties. Category is naturally a property of the edge-type node,
not a lexical convention on its URI. This lets new categories be added as data,
not code (e.g., `"derived"`, `"audit"`, `"provenance"`).

**Edge count unchanged:** 13 domain edges + 1 derived (`assesses`) + 1 system
edge (`sys:contains`, now `knm:sys_contains` with `edge_category "system"`).

**Reconciliation concerns from the original ADR still apply** — the coherence
protocol between `sys:contains` and domain `contains` is unchanged in spirit.

---

---

## Context

The knowledge graph engine needs containment relationships (e.g., "CS101 contains Variable") that carry lifecycle semantics (cascade delete, exclusivity). Simultaneously, professors need organizational relationships (e.g., grouping nodes into modules) that they can freely modify.

The question: **should these be the same edge type, or separate?**

### The Tension

A single `contains` edge serves two masters:

1. **System concern:** Data integrity — cascade delete, exclusive ownership, lifecycle management. Controlled by developers. Must always hold.
2. **Domain concern:** Organizational grouping — the professor chose to put Variable in CS101. User-authored, freely modifiable.

These look identical ("X contains Y") but have **different invariants, different owners, and change for different reasons.**

---

## Decision

**The concept `contains` exists at two distinct levels — system and domain — as separate edge types with independent semantics.** This mirrors the MDE (Model-Driven Engineering) pattern where the same concept is reused at the meta-model level (M2) and the model level (M1).

Additionally, **`teaches` is a domain edge, not a system edge.** The fact that "Prof. Chen teaches CS101" is user-authored educational data, not engine plumbing.

### The Two Levels of `contains`

| Level | Edge | Semantics | Owner | Visible | Modifiable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| System (M2) | `sys:contains` | Lifecycle ownership — cascade delete, exclusivity | Engine/developer | Hidden (power-user toggle) | No |
| Domain (M1) | `contains` | Organizational grouping — professor's course structure | Professor/user | Yes — always | Yes |

**Both express "X contains Y" but serve different masters.** The system level enforces data integrity invariants. The domain level represents the user's organizational choices. They coexist independently — a node can have `sys:contains` (lifecycle binding) without domain `contains` (not yet grouped), or vice versa.

### Full Edge Classification

| Edge | Namespace | Owner | Modifiable by user |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sys:contains` | System | Engine/developer | No — system-managed lifecycle |
| `contains` | Domain | Professor/user | Yes — organizational grouping |
| `teaches` | Domain | Professor/user | Yes — assignment data |
| `prerequisite_of`, `generalizes`, etc. | Domain | Professor/user | Yes — knowledge relationships |

**Result:** 13 formal domain edges + 1 derived (`assesses`) + 1 system edge (`sys:contains`).

---

## Rationale

A single `contains` edge conflates two concerns that change for different reasons:

| Concern | Who changes it | When | What breaks if wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sys:contains` mechanics | Developer | Engine evolution | Data integrity — orphans, accidental deletions |
| Domain `contains` grouping | Professor | Course reorganization | Workflow — things aren't where expected |

Separating them allows each to evolve independently — the system can add new lifecycle policies without constraining user organization, and users can create new grouping patterns without triggering system behaviors they didn't intend.

> **Theoretical grounding:** See thesis notes — `Thesis/Notes/namespace-architecture-rationale.md`

---

## Trade-off Accepted

**Freedom to modify independently ↔ Obligation to maintain coherence across subsystems.**

Every subsystem that touches both `sys:contains` and domain `contains` needs a reconciliation strategy. For example:

- If the professor moves a node via domain `contains` (reorganizes into a module), does `sys:contains` follow or stay?
- If the system removes a `sys:contains` edge (course deletion cascade), should domain `contains` edges to the same node also be cleaned up?
- What if domain `contains` creates a grouping that contradicts `sys:contains` exclusivity?

These coherence questions are real engineering cost. The benefit (independent modifiability, clean separation of concerns) is judged to outweigh this cost, especially for a system whose thesis contribution is precisely about knowledge graph architecture.

---

## Consequences

1. **Edge schema** must distinguish system and domain namespaces at the type level
2. **All subsystems** (traversal, visualization, inference, validation) must handle both edge types and understand which is authoritative for lifecycle vs. organizational queries
3. **User-facing UI** shows domain `contains` as the organizational view; `sys:contains` is invisible unless in power-user/debug mode
4. **Inference rules** in Jena operate on domain edges; `sys:contains` is engine-internal state
5. **Coherence protocol** needed: each subsystem that touches both levels must define reconciliation behavior (e.g., what happens when domain `contains` and `sys:contains` disagree)

---

## Affected Design Documents

| Document | Changes Required |
|---|---|
| `KNOWLEDGE_NODE_MODEL.md` | `teaches` → domain edge; add `contains` to domain edges; remove `sys:teaches` from `ThesisSystemEdge`; update Session 5 decisions |
| `phase-2-type-system/TYPE_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md` | Same edge type changes in TypeScript definitions; update system edge visual styles |
| `THESIS_DEMO_GAP_ANALYSIS.md` | "2 system edges" → "1 system edge"; update verification checklist |
| `phase-1-domain-data/DOMAIN_DATA_DESIGN.md` | Update system edge layer section; `sys:teaches` → `teaches` in data samples; update decision log |

---

## Related

- **Thesis rationale:** `Thesis/Notes/namespace-architecture-rationale.md`
- **ADR-001:** Backend and data architecture

**`knl:` = engine standard library.**

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Layer | Between `kn:` kernel and external/user namespaces |
| Holds | Engine-required edge types only |
| Membership test | **Engine-feature test:** "Does deleting this symbol break a shipped engine feature?" If yes → `knl:`. |
| Size | 5–7 symbols (small by design) |
| Examples | `knl:prerequisite_of` (Linear Traversal hardcodes), `knl:demonstrates` / `knl:is_demonstrated_by` (Problem-First hardcodes), `knl:assesses` (derived by OWL inference) |
| Owned by | Engine team, grows by ADR |
| Renamed from | `knm:` (which previously held both engine-required edges *and* a starter type catalog — split per ADR-005 addendum 2026-04-28) |
| Authoring | Shipped with engine (`standard-lib.ttl`); demos add `rdfs:domain`/`rdfs:range` constraints in their own namespace |

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Engine-feature test is the discriminator between `knl:` and user namespace. `prerequisite_of` qualifies because Linear Traversal code does `repository.followEdge("knl:prerequisite_of", ...)` — string-literal reference. `generalizes` doesn't — engine just queries "all domain edges" generically. That string-literal-in-code threshold is what makes the test mechanical.
- Domain types (`Concept`, `Course`, `Professor`) explicitly fail the test: engine treats nodes generically via `kn:type_of kn:NodeType`. So they leave `knl:` for user namespace `cs:`. The thesis claim "engine is type-agnostic" depends on this honest split.
- Stability gradient runs `kn:` (locked v1) → `knl:` (ADR-only changes) → external ontologies (community cycle) → user namespace (free authorship). `knl:` is the slowest-moving layer the engine still owns; everything more flexible lives outside.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

content.text:
Three `knl:` edges. Engine reads each by URI, hence kernel-library status.

| Edge | Direction | OWL semantics | Engine feature that hardcodes it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `knl:prerequisite_of` | `cs:Concept` → `cs:Concept` | Transitive | **Linear Traversal** — follows chain forward to build a learning path; gap detection. Reads the URI by name. |
| `knl:demonstrates` | `cs:Concept` → `cs:Principle` | Inverse pair with `knl:is_demonstrated_by` | **Problem-First Traversal** — given a Principle, finds Concepts that demonstrate it. |
| `knl:is_demonstrated_by` | `cs:Principle` → `cs:Concept` | Inverse pair with `knl:demonstrates` | **Problem-First Traversal** — symmetric counterpart. Engine generates one direction from the other via OWL `owl:inverseOf`. |

**Semantics in plain language:**

- `prerequisite_of` — "A must be understood before B can be taught." Source is the prerequisite, target is the dependent. Transitive: if A is prereq of B and B is prereq of C, A is prereq of C.
- `demonstrates` — "Concept C is an instance / illustration / proof-of of Principle P." E.g. `cs:MergeSort knl:demonstrates cs:Stability` (merge sort is a stable algorithm; it demonstrates the Stability principle).
- `is_demonstrated_by` — the reverse arrow. "Principle P is demonstrated by Concept C." Authored or inferred either direction; OWL fills in the other.

**Why these earn `knl:` while sibling edges (`generalizes`, `builds_on`, `is_component_of`) live in `cs:`:**

Engine code does literal-string lookups on these URIs. Linear Traversal's source contains something like `repo.outgoing(node, "knl:prerequisite_of")`. Sibling edges aren't named in code — they're just "all domain edges" from the engine's view. That's the engine-feature test in action.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The inverse pair (`demonstrates` / `is_demonstrated_by`) ships as **two URIs**, not one with a "direction" property. RDF predicates are inherently directed — to traverse "given a Principle, find Concepts demonstrating it" you either traverse the inverse predicate or query with the variable bindings flipped. Two URIs + `owl:inverseOf` lets the reasoner generate the missing direction so authors only write one side.
- Transitivity on `prerequisite_of` is what makes Linear Traversal cheap. Engine doesn't walk the chain manually; it asks SPARQL `?start knl:prerequisite_of+ ?reachable` (property-path) and Jena's OWL 2 RL reasoner has already materialized the closure. The reasoner does the algorithmic work; traversal code stays declarative.
- These three are the *only* edges the engine knows by name in the demo. Everything else in the curriculum (`cs:generalizes`, `cs:teaches`, `cs:contains`) the engine treats as opaque domain edges. That asymmetry is the demo's honest reckoning of how type-agnostic the engine actually is — Claim 7 (reflexivity) rests on this minimal coupling.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

content.text:
Real tension. RDF rigor vs NL fluidity. Here's how it usually gets bridged.

## What the substrate already gives you (rigid primitives that *enable* softness)

| Primitive | What it lets you express |
|---|---|
| `owl:equivalentProperty` | "X and Y are the same predicate." Reasoner unifies them. Already in your stack. |
| `rdfs:subPropertyOf` | "X is a specialization of Y." Hierarchies of relations. `cs:instructs rdfs:subPropertyOf cs:teaches`. |
| `skos:exactMatch` / `closeMatch` / `relatedMatch` | Graded alignment between concepts/predicates across vocabularies. Already used in ADR-007 for groupings. |
| `rdfs:label` (multi-language) | Same URI, multiple NL strings. `cs:teaches rdfs:label "teaches"@en, "imparte"@es, "instructs"@en`. |
| Confidence on reified edges | Edge has `cs:confidence 0.7` etc. Soft fact. Engine can filter by threshold. |

These cover **declared** synonymy. User has to author the equivalence. Doesn't auto-discover.

## What's missing — the "soft alignment" frontier

The hop you're sketching ("system spots the meta-relationship") is what ontology-alignment / KG-embedding research lives in. Three approaches that plug into the reflexive substrate cleanly:

**1. Predicate embeddings (KG-embedding-style).** Represent each `kn:EdgeType` as a vector trained on its (subject, object) co-occurrence. Two edge types with similar usage patterns get near vectors → candidate `owl:equivalentProperty`. Tools: TransE, RotatE, ComplEx.

**2. Label + example LLM alignment.** Feed predicate labels + 5 sample triples to LLM. Ask "are these synonymous?". Soft signal. Same shape as ADR-007's classification pipeline — bootstrap proposes, user approves, alignment becomes graph data.

**3. Lexicalization via OntoLex / Lemon.** W3C standard for binding NL terms to ontology entities. Lets you author "the verb 'depends on' lexicalizes `cs:prerequisite_of` (75% confidence)" as proper RDF.

The marriage pattern in all three: **NL stays soft (LLM/embedding suggests), ontology stays rigid (user-approved alignments become hard `owl:equivalentProperty` triples)**. Rigor for what's authored; softness for what's *proposed*.

## How it'd land in your demo

If you want this as future-work scaffolding (not v1):

```
NL author writes: "MergeSort uses divide-and-conquer"
                          │
                          ▼
              LLM/embedding suggests:
              cs:MergeSort cs:applies_in cs:DivideAndConquer (0.82)
              cs:MergeSort cs:is_instance_of cs:DivideAndConquer (0.61)
                          │
                          ▼
              User accepts → emits hard triple
              + optional skos:relatedMatch to "uses" predicate cluster
```

Same bootstrap-vs-population shape as ADR-007. The pipeline pattern generalizes from "categorize nodes" to "categorize relations".

## Research touchstones if you want to dig

- **Ontology Learning from Text** (Cimiano, 2006) — canonical reference for NL → ontology induction.
- **Knowledge Graph Embeddings** survey (Wang et al., 2017) — predicate vector approaches.
- **Ontology Matching** (Euzenat & Shvaiko, 2013) — schema-level alignment, including predicate alignment.
- **OntoLex-Lemon** (W3C 2016) — standard for NL ↔ ontology lexicalization.
- **Probabilistic Soft Logic / Markov Logic Networks** — soft semantics on top of rigid FOL/DL.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The "rigid vs soft" framing has a tidy resolution: **rigid is the storage shape, soft is the proposal shape**. Pipelines (LLMs, embeddings, EVōC) emit soft suggestions; user approval converts to rigid triples. Your substrate already enforces this for nodes via ADR-007. Generalizing to predicates is the same pattern at a meta-layer — and it would *itself* be a beautiful Claim 7 demonstration: the predicate-alignment system uses the same node/edge/UI machinery as the domain content.
- Predicate alignment has a peculiar property: it's **second-order**. Aligning `cs:teaches ≡ cs:instructs` is a triple *about* predicates. RDF treats this naturally because predicates are URIs and URIs can be subjects (your reflexivity foundation makes this trivial — they're already nodes). In a non-reflexive system this needs awkward escape mechanisms; in yours it's just another `kn:Edge` with `kn:type_of owl:equivalentProperty`.
- The "1 relationship kind synonymous to many" intuition has a historical name: **predicate clustering** (or relation extraction's "open IE" → canonicalization step). OpenIE systems extract NL predicates by surface form ("acquires", "purchases", "buys") and cluster to canonical relations. The ML heuristics there are battle-tested. You wouldn't need to invent the algorithm — pull from there.
- Watch for the trap of *too much* alignment. If everything ends up `owl:equivalentProperty` to everything-else, the type system collapses to a single relation and loses discriminative power. Real alignments need a confidence threshold, a human-in-the-loop gate, and probably explicit hierarchies (`subPropertyOf`) instead of pure equivalence — preserving the gradient is what keeps the system useful.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Quick framing: v1 ships the rigid storage (you already have it). The soft proposal layer is where future research and v2 features land. Bookmarks for thesis-defense "future work" rather than implementation now — though sketching the pipeline shape makes the claim defensible: "the design *admits* soft NL alignment without breaking the rigid substrate."

content.text:
Possible. No format collide if put in subfolder per session.

## Existing layout

```
copilot-session-handoff/
├── PLAN.md, SESSION_INFO.md, TODOS.md, TRANSCRIPT.md   (old session, singular)
└── checkpoints/  (numbered narrative)
```

## Proposed addition (no collision)

```
copilot-session-handoff/
├── (existing files unchanged)
├── checkpoints/
│   └── 023-step-10-and-audit-pass.md       ← new narrative
└── sessions/
    └── 2026-05-06-stage-2-reconciliation/  ← per-session bucket
        ├── transcript.jsonl                ← copy of raw JSONL
        ├── context.md                      ← session summary (decisions, edits)
        └── memory-snapshot/
            ├── MEMORY.md                   ← copy of index
            ├── feedback_communication_style.md
            └── project_reimplementation_planned.md
```

## Collision check

| Concern | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `TRANSCRIPT.md` (existing, markdown) vs `transcript.jsonl` (new, JSONL) | Different name + ext → no collide |
| `MEMORY.md` in design tree vs auto-memory MEMORY.md | Different paths → no file collide. Naming overlap risk → mitigate via `memory-snapshot/` subfolder |
| Checkpoint pattern | Continues `0NN-*.md` convention. Last = 022, next = 023 |

## Caveats

1. **Source files live in user-profile** (`C:\Users\ysz10\.claude\...`). Copying → ends up in design tree → shareable. Verify no sensitive content before sharing.
2. **Snapshot ≠ live**. Future sessions still read auto-memory from `~/.claude/...`. Copy = frozen reference, not active.
3. **Transcript size**: JSONL can be MB-scale. Check before commit if repo size matters.

`✶ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Per-session subfolder = composable. Lets multiple session handoffs coexist without name collisions. Single-flat `TRANSCRIPT.md` worked for 1 session; doesn't scale.
- Checkpoint (narrative) ≠ snapshot (raw). Reader uses checkpoint for *why*, snapshot for *exact state*. Both have value; different audiences.
- Memory snapshot drift hazard: copied today, auto-memory updates tomorrow, snapshot stale. Either re-snap on each handoff or note "snapshot date" in metadata.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
